articles.title: Asian Para Games: Sheetal Devi, Swati Chaudhary storm into archery finals, eye gold medals for India
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's para archers Sheetal Devi and Swati Chaudhary stormed into the finals of their respective events at the Asian Para Games 2026 on
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's para archers Sheetal Devi and Swati Chaudhary stormed into the finals of their respective events at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Tuesday, assuring the country of at least two medals and setting up opportunities to add to India's tally.Defending champion Sheetal continued her impressive run in the women's compound category, defeating Japan's Shinohara Aya 145-137 in the semifinal. The 19-year-old will face Singapore's Alim Nur Syahidah in the gold-medal match on October 22.Swati, making her debut at the continental multi-sport event, also booked her place in the final after beating South Korea's Lee Eunhee 6-2 in the women's W1 semifinal. She will take on China's Mengkan in the gold-medal contest, with both Indian archers now assured of at least silver medals.Sheetal continues record-breaking runSheetal, who was born without arms and shoots using her feet and shoulder, has been one of India's standout performers in para archery. The Jammu and Kashmir archer equalled the world record and set a new Asian record during qualification, underlining her credentials as she seeks to defend her title.She continued her dominant campaign in the elimination rounds, defeating Hong Kong's Chan Yuen Wah 149-134 in the pre-quarterfinals and the Philippines' Agustina Bantiloc 147-135 in the quarterfinals before overcoming Shinohara in the last four.Sheetal had also produced a record-breaking 149 against Chan, surpassing the previous world record of 148 held by Britain's Jessica Stretton.The world No. 1 will now look to cap her campaign with another gold medal. She is also scheduled to compete in the compound women's doubles semifinals alongside Payal Nag.Mixed teams progress as India suffer individual setbacksIndia also advanced to the semifinals in both the recurve and compound mixed team events. Paralympic gold medallist Harvinder Singh and Bhawna defeated Thailand 6-0 in the recurve mixed team quarterfinals, while Sheetal and Toman Kumar beat Japan 154-147 in the compound mixed team competition.However, the day brought disappointment in several individual events. Harvinder lost 5-6 to China's Yun Duo in a shoot-off in the men's recurve quarterfinals, while Bhawna went down 2-6 to Mongolia's Selengee Demberel in the women's last eight.In the men's compound event, Toman suffered a 144-149 semifinal defeat to China's Ai Xinliang and will compete for bronze. Shyam Sundar Swami had earlier lost 146-147 to Ai in the quarterfinals.With Sheetal and Swati now one victory away from gold, India will look to convert their strong performances into top-podium finishes as the para archery competition progresses.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Alemania, Francia e Italia se alían en contra de España para tratar de frenar la invasión de los coches chinos
articles.standfirst: Francia y Alemania, con el apoyo de Italia, se alían para frenar la ofensiva del coche eléctrico chino, pidiendo a Bruselas permitir los motores combustión más allá 2035 en contra de la opinión del Gobierno de España
articles.summary: Los tres grandes motores europeos se alían para frenar la ofensiva del coche eléctrico chino, pidiendo a Bruselas permitir los motores combustión más allá 2035 en contra de la opinión del Gobierno de España
articles.body: Alemania, Francia e Italia, las tres grandes potencias económicas de la Unión Europea, se han aliado para plantar cara a toda la oleada de coches eléctricos que viene de China y salvaguardar su propia industria del automóvil. En concreto, Alemania y Francia han ya alcanzado un acuerdo para exigir a Bruselas que revise el 'calendario de emisiones', de forma que se puedan seguir fabricando y vendiendo coches de combustión más allá de 2035. E Italia se ha mostrado favorable a buena parte de estas propuestas. En concreto, lo que quieren proponer es que en lugar de reducir las emisiones netas en un 100%, estas se reduzcan en un 90%, lo que daría margen a seguir vendiendo coches híbridos e incluso modelos sin ningún tipo de electrificación, aunque cuesta imaginar que para entonces se fabriquen coches que ni siquiera cuentan con una electrificación micro híbrida. No obstante, hay que tener en cuenta que la Comisión Europea ya había planteado reducir el objetivo al 90% en una propuesta presentada a finales de 2025, aunque con condiciones para compensar las emisiones restantes. Detras de este cambio de rumbo no se esconde una falta de conciencia medioambiental, sino una maniobra de supervivencia industrial. China domina todo el proceso de fabricación (lo que se conoce como la 'cadena de valor') de los coches eléctricos, desde el procesamiento de materias primas críticas (como el litio, el cobalto o el níquel) hasta la fabricación de materiales y baterías a un coste inferior al que tienen que pagarlas marcas de nuestro continente. Y eso puede poner en riesgo la supervivencia de la histórica industria del automóvil europeo. Pero también obedece a un interés por adecuarse a la realidad de nuestro mercado continental, en el que algunos países (España, por ejemplo) no terminan de aceptar del todo el coche eléctrico. En el caso de España, una de las razones que más pesa en su contra es el precio, fuera del alcance de muchísimos conductores. Pero también juegan en su contra una infraestructura de recarga que avanza muy despacio, además de otras razones como la necesidad de un garaje en el que tener un punto de recarga o la ansiedad que muchos sienten ante la autonomía. Ante este escenario, la disyuntiva abierta ahora mismo para la industria europea pasa por vender coches eléctricos con escaso margen de beneficio frente a rivales chinos o pagar multas millonarias por no cumplir los límites de emisiones. De estos tres países que promueven la revisión, Alemania y Francia lo hacen además con una intención estratégica de mutua conveniencia. Berlín consigue dar oxígeno a sus grandes fabricantes para que sigan rentabilizando la ingeniería de combustión, en la que han invertido muchísimo. Y a cambio París consigue el respaldo alemán para exigir que una parte mayoritaria de los coches sea de fabricación europea. Entre las propuestas se habla del 70% excluidas las baterías, lo que permitiría acceder a ayudas o incentivos. No obstante, la industria europea todavía no puede cantar victoria porque este pacto es de momento una intención, aunque muy firme. Para que las intenciones de este bloque se traduzcan en ley, la modificación que proponen debe ser debatida y aprobada en el Consejo Europeo y el Parlamento Europeo. Aun así, y dado el peso económico de Alemania, Francia e Italia en las instituciones, el acuerdo deja muy tocado el veto total al motor térmico y perfila un nuevo escenario en el que podamos seguir comprando coches con tubo de escape. Este acuerdo, por cierto, es contrario a la postura del Gobierno de España, que sigue apostando por mantenerse en el plan original dejando de producir y vender coches térmicos a partir de 2035.

articles.title: Who is Deepthi Jeevanji? Indian para-athlete wins 400m T20 gold with Games record
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Deepthi Jeevanji continued her impressive run in para athletics by winning gold in the women's 400m T20 event at the Asian Para Games on
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Deepthi Jeevanji continued her impressive run in para athletics by winning gold in the women's 400m T20 event at the Asian Para Games on Tuesday. The Indian clocked a Games record time of 56.36 seconds to defend her title.The 23-year-old from Telangana finished ahead of Japan's Niina Kanno, who won silver in 58.92 seconds. Kanno's compatriot Akane Kato took bronze with a time of 1:00.26.Deepthi, who also holds the Asian record, has established herself as one of India's leading para-athletes with her performances at major international events.Who is Deepthi Jeevanji?Deepthi hails from a remote village in Warangal, Telangana. Her parents are small farmers who have also worked as labourers in their village. Her talent for running was spotted when she was young. According to her athlete profile, Sports Authority of India coach N Ramesh first noticed her during a state-level athletics meet when she was 15. He recognised her potential and began training her.Deepthi later received support from badminton great Pullela Gopichand. At his suggestion, she underwent testing for intellectual disability in Hyderabad.Her journey in para athletics began to gain attention after she competed at the Asian Youth Championships in Hong Kong in 2019, where she won bronze.From a village in Telangana to the international stageDeepthi continued to improve through competitions organised by the Athletics Federation of India between 2019 and 2022. She also won gold medals in the 100m and 200m events at the Khelo India Youth Games in Guwahati in 2020.Her breakthrough at the senior international level came at the Asian Para Games in 2023, where she won gold and set Games and Asian records in the women's 400m T20 event.She went on to win gold at the 2024 Para Athletics World Championships, setting a world record of 55.07 seconds. She also won a bronze medal in the same event at the Paris Paralympics in 2024.Deepthi added another achievement to her career by winning silver at the 2025 World Championships. She has also won gold at the Indian Open in 2025 and 2026.What is the T20 category?T20 is a classification for athletes with intellectual impairments. Athletes in this category may face challenges with processing information, concentration and following race plans or tactical strategies.The role of her parents in her journeyDeepthi's success has come with strong support from her parents. She has spoken about how they stood by her ambitions even when people in their village taunted them for supporting her sporting dreams.Their support, along with years of training and hard work, has helped Deepthi rise from a village in Telangana to the top level of international para athletics.Her latest gold at the Asian Para Games, achieved in a Games record time of 56.36 seconds, is another milestone in her remarkable journey.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: The Flyers, the Penguins and the NHL Teams That Are Already Regretting Their 2026 Offseason Moves
articles.summary: The 2026-27 NHL season isn't even a month old yet, but several teams are already struggling through the early going.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 NHL season isn't even a month old yet, but several teams are already struggling through the early going.

Some of those clubs made significant moves this summer via trades and free agency, hoping to better their rosters. So far, several of those acquisitions haven't worked out as hoped.

It's still early in the season, and things could improve as those pickups adjust to their new teammates and surroundings. However, it's also possible those additions won't work out as planned.

Here's a look at five teams that could already be regretting their offseason acquisitions.

Notable offseason additions: Defensemen Bowen Byram and Ian Cole, forwards Patrick Kane, Jordan Greenway, and Cole Smith.

Chicago's rebuild has spun its wheels despite having young superstar Connor Bedard and promising youngsters like Anton Frondell and Frank Nazar in the lineup.

Management tried to speed up the process with several veteran additions, but the club stumbled out of the gate with a 3-6-0 record by Oct. 19 .

Byram was the most notable pickup, acquired with Greenway from the Buffalo Sabres on June 23. He subsequently signed a six-year contract extension with an average annual salary of $12.5 million.

The 25-year-old wanted to prove himself as a No. 1 defenseman, but the results have been underwhelming thus far.

Bedard's early absence due to a shoulder injury and the birth of Byram's twin daughters on Oct. 3 contributed to his slow start. With Bedard back in the lineup, Byram's production from the blue line should improve. For now, though, he has one point in six games as he tries to find his footing with his new club.

Kane spent the best years of his future Hall of Fame career in Chicago, and received a hero's welcome from their fans. However, the 37-year-old winger's best seasons are in the past and he can no longer carry this team as he did in his prime.

Greenway and Cole are depth additions providing a physical defensive element to Chicago's roster. Both were among the few players on the roster with positive plus/minus numbers .

Still, the focus remains on Byram and Kane. If they can't help this club make strides toward playoff contention this season, management could start to feel the heat.

Notable offseason additions: Forwards Matthew Knies, Valeri Nichushkin, Ryan Lomberg, defensemen Emil Andrae and Carson Soucy, and goaltender Cam Talbot.

After missing the playoffs for the sixth straight season , the Columbus Blue Jackets made several notable roster additions. The biggest was acquiring Knies from the Toronto Maple Leafs in a multi-player deal that sent winger Kirill Marchenko to Toronto before the start of the regular season.

Knies had an immediate positive impact with two goals and three points in his first game with the Blue Jackets. However, he was held to one assist in his next six games , while Marchenko has nine points in as many games with the Maple Leafs.

The oft-injured Nichushkin is a skillful two-way winger when healthy. However, he hasn't played up to his usual standard, managing three points in his first six games with the Blue Jackets. The 31-year-old's physical style over his 12-season career could be catching up to him.

Lomberg, Andrae, Soucy, and Talbot are depth additions. Apart from Lomberg's feisty energy , the rest haven't done much to stand out consistently for the Blue Jackets, who are off to another erratic start.

Head coach Rick Bowness ripped his players for a poor showing in an embarrassing 7-3 loss to the Florida Panthers. More lopsided losses could be in the works if the new additions fail to perform as expected.

Notable offseason additions: Forwards Erik Haula, Mats Zuccarello, Corey Perry, and defenseman Erik Gustafsson.

The retirement of longtime captain Anze Kopitar left the Kings with a big gap at center. The versatile Haula was brought in to provide short-term depth and experience at that position or on the wing if necessary.

Zuccarello and Perry were also free-agent veteran additions to provide extra depth to their forward lines. Zuccarello, 39, was coming off back-to-back 54-point seasons with the Minnesota Wild. The 41-year-old Perry had 17 goals and 37 points in 72 games split between the Kings and Tampa Bay Lightning last season.

Gustafsson, 34, was signed to bring more mobility and experience to the left side of their blueline. He also previously played under head coach Peter Laviolette. Like Haula, Zuccarello, and Perry, he came at an affordable price .

However, these additions failed to make the Kings a younger, faster team. As of Oct. 19, they were the only team without a win.

Zuccarello appeared in three games before going on injured reserve . Gustafsson was a healthy scratch for two games, and Perry had yet to dent the scoresheet. Only the 35-year-old Haula had a decent start, with three points in his first six games.

The Kings could become sellers in the trade market if they don't reverse their fortunes soon. Some of those summer additions could find themselves skating with new clubs before the March 1 trade deadline.

Notable offseason additions: Goaltender Joseph Woll, defenseman Simon Benoit, forwards Noel Acciari and Jack Studnicka.

The Philadelphia Flyers made the offseason's most impactful signing, inking Anaheim Ducks center Leo Carlsson on July 3 to a five-year offer sheet worth an average annual value of $18 million.

That deal briefly made the 21-year-old Carlsson the NHL's highest-paid player, directly contributing to the sharp increase in player salaries. It would've also given the Flyers the true first-line center they desperately needed, but the Ducks retained Carlsson by matching the offer .

Had the gambit to sign away Carlsson succeeded, the Flyers might have had a better start than a woeful 1-6-3 record in their first 10 games. He would've given them the much-needed offense that they're currently lacking, as they were outscored 34-14 during that stretch.

Getting Woll from the Toronto Maple Leafs this summer has worked out well thus far, with a 2.77 goals-against average and a .916 save percentage as of Oct. 19. As for the others, they don't bear sole responsibility for the Flyers' poor performance, but they haven't really helped either.

The Flyers did not land a comparable offensive addition after Anaheim matched Carlsson's offer sheet, although they later signed Michael Bunting.

By the time Anaheim matched the offer sheet, many of the best available players were off the market, while the asking prices for other targets were too high.

Notable offseason additions: Forwards Nick Robertson and Hendrix Lapierre, and defensemen Kaeden Korczak, Trevor van Riemsdyk, and Declan Carlile.

After exceeding expectations by reaching the playoffs last season, the Pittsburgh Penguins continue to transition toward a younger roster. Part of the process has been bringing in established NHL players in their mid-twenties , like Robertson, Lapierre, Korczak, and Carlile.

Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas knew Robertson from their days with the Toronto Maple Leafs. He got off to a promising start with two goals in the Penguins' season opener, but has managed only two more goals since.

Lapierre spent his last three seasons trying to crack a deep Washington Capitals roster. He had three points in his first two games skating on the top line with Sidney Crosby, but was moved off that line when Bryan Rust returned. He went scoreless in his next four and was a healthy scratch in their last three games.

Korczak earned more playing time as a defensive blueliner and could flourish in that role. Meanwhile, van Riemsdyk has been sidelined since Oct. 10 with a lower-body injury . Carlile began with four points in his first three games, but the 26-year-old blueliner's production has since dried up, and he's struggled defensively.

Korczak could be a solid addition for the Penguins, but the struggles of Robertson and Lapierre stand out as the Penguins stumbled through a 1-5-1 slump leading up to their Oct. 19 game with Utah. Their lack of production could become an ongoing issue if the Penguins keep sliding in the standings .

articles.title: Cleveland Browns News and Rumors 10/20/26: Forget Them Picks
articles.summary: CLEVELAND, OHIO (TheOBR.com) - Good morning, Cleveland Browns fans!THE DAILY BLOVIATIONI've rooted for many strange things in my years as a Browns fan. Karma...
articles.body:
CLEVELAND, OHIO ( TheOBR.com ) - Good morning, Cleveland Browns fans!

I've rooted for many strange things in my years as a Browns fan. Karma for Baltimore. TJ Watt going into pout mode. A swirling wind off the lake right as the other team's kicker lines up.

In 2026, I've added a new one. I root against the team Myles Garrett plays for. I don't root against Myles. I root against the Rams, which, given that Myles has been on IR since September, turns out to be a pretty fine distinction.

Back in June, the Browns sent Myles to Los Angeles for Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second and a 2029 third . The Rams did it for the reason the Rams always do it. Super Bowl LXI is at SoFi Stadium in February, and they live by a famous motto about draft picks that ESPN has to print as "F--- them picks." In September, The Athletic's Hope-O-Meter had Rams fans at 98.7 percent optimism. Browns fans checked in at 2.7.

I instantly figured the Browns first-round pick from LA was going to wind up being somewhere around the 31st or 32nd pick. With Aaron Donald coming out of retirement to play alongside Myles, the fate of the 2026 season seemed assured. The only hope, in my mind, that the pick would be higher relied on the dubious prospect of Rams QB Matthew Stafford starting to show his age.

Six weeks later, the Browns are 4-2 and tied for first in the AFC North. The Rams are 2-4 and dead last in the NFC West.

Bill Barnwell's autopsy at ESPN is worth your time if you enjoy reading about other people's problems, and I'm ashamed to say I do. The Rams lost the opener to the 49ers in Melbourne after they "tried to reimagine jet lag." They lost in Denver on a pick-six. They lost to Buffalo on Monday night when the special teams melted down. And on Sunday they lost 18-16 at home to a 1-4 Cardinals team, with Jacoby Brissett dropping back 35 times and never getting sacked.

The details are delicious, in a guilty sort of way. Matthew Stafford has gone from fourth in QBR last season to 14th. He has six interceptions in six games after throwing eight all of last year, and he ranks one spot below Deshaun Watson in passer rating, which nobody had on their bingo card in August. The defense built to terrorize quarterbacks has eight sacks. Total. Todd Monken was asked Monday why our defense is better without Myles. Smart man: " I'm not going to say that . You said that... I don't know that, because he's not here."

My favorite detail: the Rams' special teams ranked 32nd in DVOA through five weeks under coordinator Bubba Ventrone, who went to L.A. straight from Berea, where our special teams ranked 32nd last year. So we didn't just send them Myles. We threw in the kicking game at no additional charge.

Then came Monday, when Sean McVay read out an injury list that sounded like a casualty report. Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring and is out six to 10 weeks. Nose tackle Poona Ford is done for the year with a torn triceps. Kobie Turner is likely headed to IR with a groin injury. Blake Grupe, the kicker they signed after cutting the last one, tore his ACL in his debut, so they're working out Brandon McManus and Matt Prater today. And Myles, who had knee surgery in mid-September and has missed five games, won't practice this week.

Mary Kay Cabot summed it up: " First Myles Garrett, and now Davante Adams ." Zac Jackson was blunter: " The Rams are a mess and the Browns hold their first-round pick in 2027." And Jack Duffin has the math: the pick is currently No. 10 , and would be No. 5 if the Eagles hadn't, in Jack's word, "bottled" their Week 4 game against the Rams.

So the question I wanted to wrestle with this morning: does it continue?

My honest answer is probably not all the way, and I hate saying it. Barnwell makes a good case that a lot of this is bad luck. The Rams are sixth in the league in pressure rate but turn under 10 percent of those pressures into sacks, second-worst in football, and that won't hold with Aaron Donald in there and Myles eventually back. They've recovered four of 13 fumbles in their games. They're 1-3 in one-score games. And the schedule softens. CBS Sports has them at the Raiders, home against the Chargers, at Washington and at Arizona before their Week 11 bye, and favored in all four. Vegas has them as 5.5-point favorites in Las Vegas this week.

Then again, no team in the Super Bowl era has had a losing record after six weeks and won its conference. ESPN's FPI has dropped the Rams' playoff chances from 83.1 percent to 35.3, with less than a 1 percent chance of winning a division where San Francisco improved to 6-0 last night. After the bye, they get the Packers, Chiefs, at San Francisco, Cowboys, at Seattle, at Tampa and Seattle again. That's not a soft finish for a 38-year-old quarterback and a kicker to be named later.

Here's the part that matters to us. Non-playoff teams pick 1 through 18. If FPI is close, there's about a two-in-three chance the Rams miss the playoffs and that pick lands in the top 18. If they sneak in as a wild card, it slides into the 20s. If the wheels really come off, we're talking about a top-10 pick in a year the Browns are shopping for a quarterback, and Mel Kiper just told Arch Manning to " go back to college for another year ." If the shelf of available quarterbacks gets thinner, the extra first gets more valuable.

Which brings me to Marktroy's Watercooler thread: " The Rams will want Jeudy with Adams gone . Do you trade him?"

No. And not only because Monken said Monday, "We're better with Jerry than we are without Jerry," or because Daryl Ruiter notes Jeudy has helped win half the games that were on the line late. The last thing I want to do in October is sell the Rams a receiver. If Les Snead calls, Andrew Berry should let it go to voicemail.

So I'll be rooting for the Raiders on Sunday, which isn't something a Browns fan of my vintage says lightly after Red Right 88 was burned into my 17-year-old brain. I'm not rooting for anybody's hamstring. I'm rooting for Las Vegas. That's as low as I'll go.

44 YARDS, NOT 45: Monken on the first half against Baltimore: "I don't want 45 yards at halftime; maybe, I guess it's 44. I better not tack on a yard there." Scott Petrak has the numbers : Watson has been sacked a league-high 24 times and thrown only two interceptions, and his four fourth-quarter scoring drives tie Josh Allen and Bo Nix for the league lead. Watson: "One of these weeks it's going to click." I'd settle for the first quarter.

The Browns open as 1.5-point favorites at Tennessee with a total of 36.5. Vegas has watched our first halves. Monken says it's too early to tell on Mason Graham, Dylan Sampson, Quinshon Judkins, Mike Hall Jr. and Grant Delpit, per Fred Greetham .

QUICKLY: Fred has Monken on the "connected" defense , John Taylor has his Monday Morning Postmortem , and VIPs get Jack Duffin's Stock Up/Down and Sam Penix's Watson accuracy charting. Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots in his lungs, and our Crap Pile folder is already full of Shedeur-to-Philly speculation with nobody credentialed attached.

Have a good one! GO BROWNS! (And go Raiders. Just this once.)

Positive news from the world of sports and beyond...

Prime Video unveiled the new trailer at New York Comic-Con, and the eight-episode series lands Nov. 25. This time the replicants won the uprising and run the show, and they're the ones hunting humans. Michelle Yeoh plays Olwen, a fading replicant Blade Runner, who teams up with Hunter Schafer's Cora, a human on the run. Space.com is excited about the off-world planets and starships, and I'm excited about Michelle Yeoh in anything. It's set in a gloomy Los Angeles at the edge of the 22nd century where nothing goes right for the people in charge. Prime Video says it's fiction. I've been reading about the Rams all morning, so I have my doubts.

When not reading Bill Barnwell's Rams autopsy for the third time, Barry McBride is the Publisher and Founder of the OBR and bloviates this nonsense every morning. You can follow him on Twitter @barrymcbride or write him at barry@theobr.com if you are so compelled.

articles.title: Mathias Beck re-elected as president
articles.summary: Eintracht Frankfurt members have chosen Mathias Beck as club president again by an overwhelming result.In his election speech, Mathias Beck set out his visio...
articles.body:
Eintracht Frankfurt members have chosen Mathias Beck as club president again by an overwhelming result.

In his election speech, Mathias Beck set out his vision and aims for the next four years to the roughly 1,400 members in attendance. It will be Beck's first full term as president, having succeeded Peter Fischer two and a half years ago.

Beck painted a clear picture of how he imagines Eintracht in the coming years, the milestones he wants to hit and what is required to achieve them. With steady growth in the membership of the club's more than 50 sport sections and fan department, the 55-year-old is looking to reach the mark of 200,000 members. To support the growth in sport, particular attention will be paid to sports facilities infrastructure. He stressed that this will require cooperation with the State of Hesse and the City of Frankfurt.

Other key areas include the modernisation of the organisation, promotion of volunteering as well as social responsibility beyond the sport. With regards to professional football, Beck outlined the future path, emphasised the importance of collaboration between the e.V. (registered association) and AG (corporation), and spoke unequivocally in favour of the 50+1 rule.

"It's been a long and emotional evening," he said. "I thank the members for the confidence placed in me and the overwhelming vote. I perform this role and the duties involved with great enthusiasm. There is much to do in many areas of Eintracht. I have clear ideas about what I want to achieve with this club and with you in the coming years."

Treasurer hands over with record results

Vice-president and treasurer Dominik Berker provided the members with detailed insights into the 2025/26 financial year, which was hugely successful. The club achieved a net income of 2.7 million euros after tax – the highest ever. Crucial to that were increased income from the trade mark licence agreement, higher membership contributions and increased sponsorship income.

"Together, we have put the finances of our club on a stable footing in recent years and made important decisions for the future," summarised Berker in his final speech as treasurer. "I am stepping down from my post with the satisfaction that the club is in an excellent position, both financially and structurally; that the tax audits for previous years have been completed; and that the financial accounting system has been almost entirely digitised. Furthermore, we can report record turnover and a record annual profit." Berker had already decided before the general meeting that he would not stand for another term.

Executive committee set to remain in current form

Beck's executive committee should comprise current vice-presidents Moritz Theimann, Armin Kraaz, Stefan Minden and Benjamin von Loefen. In accordance with the articles of association, the vice-presidents are appointed by the election committee and the supervisory board, at the suggestion of the president and following the general meeting. A decision is expected by the end of October.

articles.title: ‘Nobody is…’ – Dave Portnoy points out ‘ridiculous’ decision by San Francisco 49ers
articles.summary: Dave Portnoy states his problem with one thing the San Francisco 49ers’ offensive unit does, which he finds to be quite meaningless. The San Francisco 49ers...
articles.body:
Dave Portnoy states his problem with one thing the San Francisco 49ers' offensive unit does, which he finds to be quite meaningless.

The San Francisco 49ers are the first team to win six straight games this season after they beat the Washington Commanders on Monday night. The team has looked quite unstoppable so far, with the defense locked in and the offence humming.

Kyle Shanahan is known to be someone who likes to build team culture around leadership and accountability. Many of the 49ers' stars have been with the team for many years now and take on important roles within the locker room. Dave Portnoy has a problem with one aspect of this.

Dave Portnoy calls out San Francisco 49ers for having five 'captains' on the offensive unit

The Niners have named five captains on offence this season. They are quarterback Brock Purdy, running back Christian McCaffrey, fullback Kyle Juszczyk, tight end George Kittle and left tackle Trent Williams. This includes the cornerstone pieces of the attacking unit, alongside their most senior members.

While the quarterback remains the leader, this group's overarching task is to ensure that everything about their offence functions smoothly. Considering that there are only 11 players on the field at one time for the O, though, Dave Portnoy thinks this is excessive.

"The 49ers have five captains on offence. Basically half their offence is captains. That's ridiculous. If everybody is a captain nobody is a captain," the Barstool Sports owner posted on X during Monday night's game.

While Portnoy has something of a point, making it about the 6-0 Niners is a bit absurd. They are one of the league's best teams, and their systems are clearly working. If he tempered his takes taking anything like that into account, though, he wouldn't really be the personality he is.

articles.title: New guide, new glory! Simran storms to Games-record gold as Tejalben adds bronze at Asian Para Games
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's Simran scripted a golden comeback at the Asian Para Games 2026, setting a new Games record to win the women's 200m T12 title with her
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's Simran scripted a golden comeback at the Asian Para Games 2026, setting a new Games record to win the women's 200m T12 title with her new guide Shivam, while compatriot Tejalben Damor added a bronze to complete a memorable outing for the country on Tuesday.The 26-year-old Simran clocked 24.80 seconds to claim her maiden gold at the continental showpiece, finishing ahead of Iran's Hajar Safarzadeh, who took silver in 25.02 seconds. Tejalben, making her debut at the Asian Para Games, secured bronze with a time of 25.23 seconds.The T12 classification is for athletes with moderate visual impairment.Simran shines with new guide after difficult transitionA bronze medallist at the 2024 Paris Paralympics, Simran has been rebuilding her campaign with Shivam after her previous guide, Umar Saifi, was banned for a doping violation.She had won silver in the same event at the 2023 Hangzhou edition, making Tuesday's record-breaking performance a significant milestone in her comeback.Simran, however, admitted that fatigue and recovery issues had affected her preparations. Her personal Asian record of 24.46 seconds remained beyond reach, but she was delighted to secure the gold."My body was not feeling good, in fact, it felt tight because the recovery has not been great. I was very tired after my heat race," she said.The sprinter also spoke about the challenge of finding suitable vegetarian food at the Games, adding with characteristic humour: "Otherwise, we Indians can run on willpower too."Simran will next compete in the women's 100m, an event in which she won silver at the previous edition.Tejalben's bronze boosts confidence ahead of 400mTejalben's podium finish provided another boost to India's medal campaign. The 24-year-old said her journey had been shaped by financial hardships faced by her family and that she had arrived with considerable determination."My parents have struggled financially for most of their lives and I would even die to get a medal," she said.The bronze has strengthened her confidence ahead of the women's 400m, which she considers her strongest event."My next race is 400m and that is my best event and this medal has given me a lot of confidence for that event," Tejalben added.With Simran's gold and Tejalben's bronze, India enjoyed a double-podium finish in the women's 200m T12, highlighting the country's growing strength in para-athletics.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Former Manchester United manager Erik Ten Hag has no love lost for Cristiano Ronaldo. A few years ago, before Ronaldo’s transfer to Saudi Arabia’s Al-Nassr,...
articles.body:
Former Manchester United manager Erik Ten Hag has no love lost for Cristiano Ronaldo . A few years ago, before Ronaldo's transfer to Saudi Arabia's Al-Nassr, he was with his former club, Manchester United. However, toward the end of his run with "The Red Devils," things started to get heated between him and Ten Hag.

However, their animosity ended with the departure of the duo. Now, years later, Ten Hag has reopened his feud with Ronaldo. The former Manchester United manager shared new details about the tension between the two and how Ronaldo let his team down.

Ten Hag assumed control at Old Trafford in the summer of 2022. In his debut season, he secured the English League Cup and later won the FA Cup in 2024, prior to being sacked in October of that year.

articles.title: Redmond’s Kristina Liutova reaches Edmond Open final, falls to Sloane Stephens
articles.summary: Redmond’s Kristina Liutova reached the Edmond Open W100 final in Edmond, Oklahoma on Sunday after returning to action last week for the first time since her...
articles.body:
Redmond's Kristina Liutova reached the Edmond Open W100 final in Edmond, Oklahoma on Sunday after returning to action last week for the first time since her first-round U.S. Open loss in September.

Liutova, 16, won her first four matches in straight sets before losing Sunday's final to 2017 U.S. Open champion Sloane Stephens, 3-6, 2-6.

Stephens, 33, had not won a title since April 2024. She reached a career-high ranking of No. 3 in 2018 and is now ranked No. 118 following Sunday's win.

Stephens has been working her way back up the tennis rankings after suffering a stress fracture in her right foot in 2025. Earlier in her career, she suffered a similar injury in her left foot.

By reaching the Edmond Open final, Liutova climbed six spots in the rankings to No. 110.

Kristina Liutova's Memphis Classic breakthrough

Liutova entered the Memphis Classic over the summer ranked No. 229 in the world. She fought through qualifying and won the tournament, becoming the youngest active WTA champion and the first person born in the 2010s to win a tour-level event. It was the first tour-level event she had ever played.

Liutova's mother, Elena Morozova, said her daughter has been competitive since birth.

"Even when she played hide-and-seek, she wanted to win every time. Even when she played chess with her dad, she wanted to win every time," Morozova said. "In everything she was doing, she was trying to win."

On the court, Liutova doesn't focus on results. Her mentality is to put in the work and let the scoreboard take care of itself — the same mentality as her tennis hero.

"My favorite tennis player has always been Rafael Nadal, for his composure, for his hardworking character," Liutova said. "He's been through a lot of injuries, and the character is just shown in everything. He is just a great human as well, off the court. Always humble. Just an incredibly inspiring person and player."

Liutova is keeping her overall tennis goals and dreams private for now. But she wants to inspire others and take care of her mom, who has sacrificed so much to get her where she is today.

"I want to make sure that she's happy, and in the future, she has an easy life — a house, a cat — and just watch my matches with no worries and no pressure," Liutova said.

Liutova's U.S. Open run ends against Zheng Qinwen

After Memphis, Liutova won three U.S. Open qualifying matches in New York to reach the main draw . There, she faced 2024 Olympic gold medalist Zheng Qinwen. Liutova couldn't hold off the veteran, falling 4-6, 6-3, 6-1.

Liutova left the court in tears after her nine-match winning streak ended.

ESPN match commentator Robbie Koenig offered Liutova words of encouragement.

"I'll tell you what, there will be a lot more tears of joy in the years to come," Koenig said after her U.S. Open loss. "That's for sure, given the game that she possesses. Don't worry about that, Kristina."

Kristina Liutova makes Grand Slam main-draw history

Liutova fought through three qualifying matches to earn a place in the U.S. Open main draw.

"[She's] just so accurate with her ball striking," Koenig said of Liutova early in the match. "I'm gobsmacked that she's just 16 years of age."

Liutova is the first player born in the 2010s to qualify for a Grand Slam tournament's main draw. She was also the youngest person in the draw.

"Honestly, I never look at the stats," Liutova told KIRO Newsradio before the U.S. Open. "When I get told, I forget immediately."

Zheng acknowledged the teenager during her post-match ESPN interview.

"I want to say congratulations first to the opponent because she's only 16 years old," Zheng said. "Very young junior, and she played incredible tennis. Fights a lot. It was not easy for me."

Frank Lenzi is the News Director for KIRO Newsradio. Read more of his stories here .

articles.title: Crimson Crank: Nitpicking Indiana’s 19-15 loss to Ohio State
articles.summary: The problems that led to Indiana’s loss to Ohio State, largely on offense, had been brewing for weeks before the game.
articles.body:
Indiana suffered its first loss since 2024 on Saturday afternoon, falling to Ohio State 19-15. It was a hard-fought game between two evenly-matched teams, as reflected by the the fact that the Hoosiers fell just one spot in the latest AP Poll.

Because of how winnable the game was, fans and media alike have spent much of the last two days trying to figure out who to blame, particularly for Indiana's final offensive play. After struggling for most of the day, Josh Hoover threw a ball that was good, but not great, to Nick Marsh, who caught it with his feet out of bounds to effectively end the game.

It's a painful play to revisit, even as I sit here thinking about it Monday evening. But was that really what cost Indiana the game? Not really.

I was critical of the passing game on Saturday because the accuracy issues predated the Ohio State game. Indiana punted four times, in addition to the two field goal tries, because drives kept stalling out when Hoover missed passes. Any one of these could have ended in the touchdown that would have won the game for the Hoosiers.

Then there are the missed field goals. Radicic missing an easy one had an immeasurable impact on the game. Had he converted from 32 yards out, Indiana's final drive wouldn't have had to end with a shot at the end zone. The drive could have been planned around just getting into Radicic's normally consistent range.

It's not fair to blame Radicic for the miss from 55-yards, but it's another play – more so than the Hoover's last pass – worthy of a closer look.

After the Nebraska game, I questioned whether Cignetti had lost some of the aggression that made last year so special. The decision to kick down six from well beyond Radicic's career-long only makes me worry more.

Because Radicic had never really given us reason to think this was in his range, I struggle with calling this the "safe" call from Cignetti. It's kind of just a head-scratcher.

I watched Indiana's offense on Saturday, like everyone else, so I do understand lacking confidence in execution on a crucial fourth down play. That said, there are going to be other high-leverage plays this season that the offense will need to execute on, so they may as well practice now.

With how much Indiana has struggled to run the ball the last few weeks, the staff may have felt somewhat handcuffed in play-calling, which could have impacted the decision. The defense was also playing well, making a turnover feel less threatening in that scenario.

Saturday's result, though, demonstrates that offenses have to make plays to win games. Whether it's Hoover settling down and making passes that he's capable of making, or Mike Shanahan retooling the run game to get Lee Beebe Jr. and Turbo Richard some better looks, it's not a problem Indiana can shy away from.

I don't pretend to have an answer, but taking a step back from Saturday makes it clear that the loss has more to do with issues that have been plaguing Indiana's offense well before the Buckeyes got to town. If Indiana can clean these things up and string together more scoring drives, there will be no reason to litigate single incompletions.

articles.title: Indiana’s Malia Samuels lands NIL deal with World’s Finest Chocolate
articles.summary: Indiana Hooiser Malia Samuels explains why her new NIL partnership is so important to her.
articles.body:
Many college athletes view NIL deals as opportunities to support good causes.

Indiana women's basketball player Malia Samuels' new NIL deal with World's Finest Chocolate is one of those feel-good stories of giving back.

World's Finest Chocolate is a fundraising company that helps schools, sports teams, clubs, and community organizations raise money by giving youth the opportunity to sell chocolate. From third to fifth grade, Samuels sold WFC's chocolate to fund travel basketball opportunities and follow her dream.

Now she is a "Reign Maker" for the company's "Let Them Reign" campaign.

She is the first female college athlete to partner with the brand.

As explained by the CEO of World's Finest Chocolate , Eddie Opler, in a press release:

"Let Them Reign" was created to celebrate the ambition behind fundraising and the experiences it can help make possible. Having Malia join us as our first female NIL partner marks an important chapter for the campaign. We're proud to have her represent what can happen when determination, opportunity, and support come together.

The campaign focuses on encouraging youth to develop confidence, communication skills, resilience and entrepreneurial thinking while selling the chocolate.

Samuels herself used her childhood experience with World's Finest Chocolates to break out of her shell and improve her communication skills.

The basketball it allowed her to play led to her becoming the No. 1 recruit from her home state of Washington in 2023. In high school in Seattle, she won two state championships and received the 3A Washington State Player of the Year award as a junior in 2022. After three years at USC, she is excited to suit up for the Hoosiers in 2026-27.

Samuels took the time to speak with Swish Appeal about the deal.

Yeah for sure, it was definitely gratifying, kind of to help my parents out. And I think it was more so fun for me to do than thinking about, "Oh I have to do this to play travel basketball." It was just something that me and my teammates would kind of try to compete and see who could sell the most chocolate and stuff like that. But looking back, it was definitely gratifying.

Yeah for sure. I think basketball has always been such a big part of my life. And without the travel basketball piece from when I was really young, I wouldn't be where I'm at now. So I do have a lot of gratitude toward World's Finest Chocolate for making that happen for me.

I think I've always tried to use my NIL for a good cause, whether that be my camps that I did last year or finding a good cause to give back to my community. Just because the high school that I went to was in a kind of rough area of the city. I want kids to kind of like see themselves in me and want to do this when they get to my age and give back to kids. I want the generations to just keep building on each other and giving back to each other.

I think for me, it taught me skills that I didn't realize were so valuable. Like communication, confidence and resilience. Being ok with some nos because ultimately some nos will lead to some yeses. I think it's very important to teach kids those skills at such a young age. I think COVID kind of messed that up for some kids and their development. So I think it's important to really hone in and focus on the fundamental skills that kids need now.

I think it's super significant, and I think for me it has even more significance because I was on a boys' basketball team when I did sell chocolate. There weren't like a ton of girls around playing sports. There weren't a lot of girls that took basketball seriously at that age. So I had to play with the boys.

So it's super significant for girls to get more opportunities, for women's basketball to get more popular. Having the opportunity to travel and do all these things with basketball, it kind of shows girls all around the world that, "Oh this is really something." And that's kind of my basketball story. Like, "Oh I can go to college and play basketball?" Like, I never knew that. So I think that's kind of what I want to be for the next generation of girls by doing this.

articles.title: SailGP inaugura su primera base de entrenamiento permanente en Florida
articles.standfirst: En palabras de Dylan Fletcher, piloto del equipo británico, supone un punto de inflexión
articles.summary: En palabras de Dylan Fletcher, piloto del equipo británico, supone un punto de inflexión
articles.body: SailGP ha inaugurado oficialmente su primera base de entrenamiento en el vanguardista American Magic High Performance Center de Pensacola en Florida. Los primeros deportistas de SailGP y el catamarán F50 han llegado para marcar el inicio de una nueva era en las carreras de alto rendimiento. A partir de esta semana, las instalaciones de Pensacola funcionarán como un centro de entrenamiento centralizado y abierto todo el año para la flota internacional y regatistas en formación. Su inauguración supone un hito fundamental para el campeonato mundial de carreras náuticas: un ecosistema de alto rendimiento abierto todo el año destinado a acelerar el desarrollo de los deportistas, reforzar la integridad competitiva y apoyar el crecimiento de este deporte. El acuerdo multi-temporada para la base de entrenamiento, vigente hasta 2031, supone una alianza estratégica entre American Magic y SailGP, dos referentes en las carreras náuticas de élite. “Pensacola ofrece condiciones estables y unas instalaciones de primer nivel que permitirán a nuestros equipos hacer pruebas, entrenar e innovar continuamente para garantizar que las carreras náuticas sigan siendo las más emocionantes del mundo”, dijo Andrew Thompson, director general de SailGP. Por su parte, Tyson Lamond, Chief Operating Officer de American Magic, se mostró encantado con el acuerdo: "Este compromiso de cinco años nos brinda la oportunidad de hacer partícipe de la emoción de SailGP a más gente de la zona. Junto con nuestros partners comunitarios, esperamos crear experiencias que Pensacola pueda compartir y celebrar durante muchos años". Dylan Fletcher, piloto de Emirates GBR SailGP Team que ha sido uno de los primeros deportistas en probar la base de entrenamiento, afirmó: "Disponer de unas instalaciones específicas como las de Pensacola para realizar pruebas, entrenar e innovar fuera de los fines de semana de competición supondrá un punto de inflexión para los deportistas de SailGP. Nos brinda la oportunidad de superar realmente los límites, ajustar nuestras comunicaciones y perfeccionar nuestras estrategias. Las condiciones en la bahía de Pensacola serán fantásticas, y contar con esta base centralizada elevará sin duda el nivel de la competición y la profundidad de toda la flota". La base de entrenamiento de SailGP funcionará siguiendo unas normas constantes para reforzar el compromiso de la liga con la equidad deportiva. Todos los equipos tendrán el mismo acceso a reservar bloques de entrenamiento fuera de los fines de semana de competición a medida que el campeonato siga expandiéndose a nivel mundial.

articles.title: India’s medal storm! 24 medals, five golds as Nishad Kumar, Deepthi Jeevanji shine at Asian Para Games
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India produced a stunning medal rush on Day 2 of the Asian Para Games 2026, collecting 24 medals, including five golds, as athletics powered
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India produced a stunning medal rush on Day 2 of the Asian Para Games 2026, collecting 24 medals, including five golds, as athletics powered the country's campaign in Aichi-Nagoya on Tuesday. Nishad Kumar headlined the action with a second gold in as many days, while Deepthi Jeevanji reaffirmed her continental supremacy with a Games-record triumph.At the end of the day's competition, India occupied sixth place in the standings with 35 medals — nine gold, 11 silver and 15 bronze. Athletics accounted for 20 of India's medals so far, underlining its importance to the country's campaign.Alongside the established stars, emerging athletes also delivered encouraging performances, while archery and badminton provided further reasons for optimism by assuring India of more medals in the coming days.Nishad, Deepthi lead India's golden chargeNishad became only the third Indian to win two gold medals in a single edition of the Asian Para Games after adding the men's high jump T47 title to his long jump gold from Monday. The two-time Paralympic silver medallist cleared 2.04m to establish a new Games record.He joined Ankur Dhama and armless archer Sheetal Devi, who had each won two golds at the 2023 Hangzhou edition.Deepthi set the tone early, winning the women's 400m T20 title in a Games-record time of 56.36 seconds. The 23-year-old from Telangana, a former world champion and Paris Paralympics bronze medallist, secured her second consecutive Asian Para Games gold in the event.The golden run continued with Simran winning the women's 200m T12 title in a Games-record 24.80 seconds. Despite struggling with fatigue and limited vegetarian food options, the Paralympic bronze medallist delivered a commanding performance. Games debutant Tejalben Damor added bronze in the same event with a personal-best 25.23 seconds.Pranav Soorma claimed gold in the men's discus throw combined F51/52/53 event with an Asian-record effort of 11.66m, while compatriot Ram Ratan Singh took silver with 10.35m. Devender Kumar completed India's five-gold haul for the day by winning the men's discus throw F44/64 event.Shooting, powerlifting and swimming add to the haulIndia collected two medals in shooting, with Manish Narwal winning silver in the men's 10m air pistol SH1 event and Shrishti Arora taking bronze in the women's 10m air pistol SH1 competition.Narwal, a Paris 2024 Paralympics silver medallist, shot 233.7 in the final to finish behind South Korea's Jo Jeongdu. His performance also secured India a quota place for the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics. India's shooting tally rose to four medals after two days, comprising one gold, two silver and one bronze.In powerlifting, Ashok Kumar Malik won silver in the men's 65kg category with a best lift of 192kg. The 37-year-old from Haryana improved on the bronze he won at the previous edition.Swimming contributed two more bronze medals. Himanshu Nandal, who was born blind due to optic nerve failure, clocked 5:10.91 to finish third in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event. Niranjan Mukundan followed with bronze in the men's 200m individual medley SM7, finishing in 2:57.01.Para table tennis also delivered a landmark performance. Ravi Baby Sahana and Prachi Pandey became the first Indian players to win medals in the standing category at the Asian Para Games. They were joined on the podium by Paralympics medallist Bhavina Patel, Sonalben Patel and Jehan Madan, taking India's haul to five bronze medals in the competition.Bhavina lost to China's Zhang Bian in the Class 4-5 semifinal, while Sonalben went down to South Korea's Jiyu Yoon in Class 3. Sahana lost to China's Mao Jingdian in Class 9, and Prachi was beaten by Iraq's Najlah Al-Dayyeni in Class 6.Archery assures five medals; badminton stars reach last fourIndia's medal tally is set to grow further, with para archery assuring the country of at least five medals through finalists across individual, doubles and mixed-team events.Defending champion Sheetal Devi stormed into the women's compound final after defeating Japan's Shinohara Aya 145-137. Sheetal, who equalled the world record and set a new Asian record in qualification, will face Singapore's Alim Nur Syahidah for gold.Games debutant Swati Chaudhary also assured India of at least silver after beating South Korea's Eunhee Lee 6-2 in the women's W1 semifinal.India's women's compound doubles pair of Sheetal and Payal Nag defeated Thailand's Phannibha Srathongmaew and Wasana Khuthawisap 151-135 to reach the gold-medal match. Pooja and Bhawna advanced to the women's recurve doubles final with a 6-2 win over Iran's Mohadeseh Babahabib and Rahimi Ghahderijani Somayeh. Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi also progressed to the men's recurve doubles final after edging South Korea 5-4.The recurve mixed team of Harvinder and Bhawna defeated Thailand 6-0 to reach the semifinals, while Sheetal and Toman Kumar advanced in compound mixed team after beating Japan 154-147.Badminton also guaranteed India more medals. World champion Pramod Bhagat defeated Japan's Daisuke Fujihara 21-12, 21-10 to reach the men's singles SL3 semifinals, extending his record of podium finishes at the Para Asiad to five consecutive editions. He will face South Korea's Lee Seunghu on Thursday.Paralympic gold medallist Kumar Nitesh also advanced to the last four after beating compatriot Vikram Kumar 21-8, 21-8. He will meet Indonesia's Al Muh Imran in the semifinal.With five golds already secured on Tuesday and more medals assured in archery and badminton, India ended Day 2 with momentum firmly on their side as the campaign gathered pace in Aichi-Nagoya.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ronnie O'Sullivan: Why seven-time world champion faces a battle to stay in world's top 16
articles.summary: Snooker's World Championship without Ronnie O'Sullivan is hard to conceive, after years of him being so often the central figure at the Crucible. But it may not be far away.
articles.body:
A snooker World Championship without Ronnie O'Sullivan?

The prospect seems almost unthinkable, with the 50-year-old a near ever present in the top 16 of the world rankings since he became a professional in 1992.

However, the seven-time winner at the Crucible now faces a battle to maintain his place within the 16-man group guaranteed automatic entry to the World Championship.

Already down at number 13 in the world rankings, O'Sullivan fell in the first round of the Northern Ireland Open on Monday and is in need of prize money that would solidify his place among the current world elite.

Still seeking the eighth world title that would mean he surpasses former rival Stephen Hendry, O'Sullivan has said he would prefer to retire rather than ever enter qualifying events.

With a challenging decision potentially looming, BBC Sport takes a look at how close one of the sport's greats is to leaving the game forever.

O'Sullivan has had a quiet start to the 2026-27 season, with a run to the semi-finals of the Wuhan Open the only significant result in his five tournaments to date.

Two last-16 finishes preceded his final-four finish at that event, but he has been defeated in the first round in his two subsequent appearances, in Shenzhen and Belfast.

Having earned £513,750 at ranking events over two years, O'Sullivan is £99,350 ahead of Ali Carter, who holds 16th spot in the world rankings, and £154,650 clear of Zhou Yuelong, who sits in 17th, with winnings of £359,100.

On first glance, that appears to be a comfortable cushion, with only a set of significant runs from his rivals putting him at risk of having to qualify for the World Championships in May next year.

However, there are issues over the horizon, because over a third of O'Sullivan's winnings come from reaching the final of the Saudi Arabia Masters in August 2025.

The £200,000 he won in Jeddah will continue to count towards his ranking past the 2027 World Championship, but that money will slip out of the eligibility period soon after the start of the 2027-28 season.

O'Sullivan will also not be able to replace his earnings with another run at the event, after the tournament, which offered the highest prize money outside of UK-based competitions, was abolished in April.

That means he is likely to need strong performances over the next 18 months to remain in contention for an automatic spot at the 2028 World Championship.

Should O'Sullivan appear at more tournaments?

O'Sullivan might improve his chances of earning ranking prize money by competing in more tournaments, having operated on a reduced schedule in recent years.

It should be noted he has cited medical reasons or the need to prioritise his mental health for his withdrawals from several tournaments in recent years.

He played predominantly in Asia in 2025-26, only competing in two tournaments in Britain - the UK Championship and World Championship.

His appearance in Belfast this week was his first in a ranking event in the United Kingdom outside the Triple Crown events (Masters, World Championship, UK Championship) since the English Open in September 2024.

His last ranking title came at the World Grand Prix in January of the same year.

After his defeat in the semi-finals of the Wuhan Open in August, O'Sullivan said he did not "want to throw in the towel just yet".

But he has also acknowledged he has limited time left in the sport, giving himself until 2028 , external to beat Hendry's world title total by landing an eighth.

Should he slip out of the top 16, O'Sullivan has said he has no interest in competing in World Championship qualifying - held this year at the English Institute of Sport in Sheffield - stating he would retire from snooker instead.

There are 16 places available for the World Championship through the qualifying rounds, with Hendry, Mark Williams, Ding Junhui and Steve Davis among players past and present who have taken that route after slipping out of the elite 16 amid declining results.

It seemingly holds no appeal to O'Sullivan, though.

"I'd love to win another World Championship. I've got two attempts at it," O'Sullivan told World Snooker Tour in July.

"If I don't do it this season or the next season, then it'll definitely never happen.

"I'm not going to play qualifiers. You won't be seeing me go down to Barnsley trying to win qualifying matches and all that sort of stuff.

"I have to be realistic. If that happens, then obviously that's the end of my career. But hopefully, I can keep going for at least another two seasons."

Playing in more tournaments may be the most obvious way to avoid a difficult retirement decision, but O'Sullivan has spoken candidly about his battles with depression and anxiety and may feel he cannot compete more regularly.

O'Sullivan has threatened to retire on multiple occasions during his career before deciding to stick with the sport, going back as far as his teenage years.

Those have usually quickly been forgotten and the reality is that he has displayed remarkable longevity, with his first World Championship win coming in 2001 and his latest in 2022.

However, faced with fading powers and a resulting lack of prize money, we may be entering the end stage of the all-time great's career.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a spectacular medal rush at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Tuesday, winning 24 medals, including five golds, but the impressive haul was not enough to prevent the country from slipping from fourth to sixth in the standings as rivals also enjoyed a bumper day in Aichi-Nagoya.India finished Day 2 with 35 medals — nine gold, 11 silver and 15 bronze — after adding five gold, six silver and 13 bronze medals to Monday's tally. However, the medal table is ranked primarily by the number of gold medals won, followed by silver and bronze, rather than the overall medal count.That distinction proved crucial. South Korea moved to fourth with 12 gold medals, while Iran climbed to fifth with 10. India, with nine golds, dropped to sixth despite having more medals than South Korea.China widen gap as Uzbekistan overtake JapanChina continued to dominate the competition, extending their lead at the top with 70 gold medals and 149 medals overall. The gap between China and the chasing nations remained substantial, with Uzbekistan in second place on 17 golds and 56 medals.Hosts Japan, despite having 63 medals — seven more than Uzbekistan — occupied third place with 16 golds. Uzbekistan's superior gold count kept them ahead.Thailand were seventh with 41 medals, including eight golds. Kazakhstan, Indonesia and Malaysia completed the top 10 in the standings.India's position was therefore not a reflection of a poor day. Rather, the competition at the top intensified as rival nations accumulated gold medals at a faster rate.ALSO READ: India’s medal storm! 24 medals, five golds as Nishad Kumar, Deepthi Jeevanji shineNishad, Deepthi lead India's golden chargeIndia's five gold medals on Tuesday came through an outstanding athletics performance, led by Nishad Kumar and Deepthi Jeevanji.Nishad won the men's high jump T47 title with a Games-record clearance of 2.04m, adding to his long jump gold from Monday. He became only the third Indian to win two gold medals in a single edition of the Asian Para Games.Deepthi reaffirmed her continental supremacy by winning the women's 400m T20 gold in a Games-record time of 56.36 seconds.Simran claimed the women's 200m T12 title in a Games-record 24.80 seconds, while Pranav Soorma won the men's discus throw combined F51/52/53 event with an Asian-record effort of 11.66m. Devender Kumar completed India's gold rush by winning the men's discus throw F43/64 event.The five golds provided a significant boost, but India's six silver and 13 bronze medals also contributed heavily to the 24-medal haul. The country's overall tally rose from 11 to 35 in just one day.India will look to convert its strong performances in archery and badminton into further medals in the coming days. articles.title: Dan Quinn's fourth-down explanation exposes a different failure of attention to detail
articles.summary: After Monday night's game, Commanders coach Dan Quinn took his time in showing up to talk to reporters.
articles.body:
After Monday night's game, Commanders coach Dan Quinn took his time in showing up to talk to reporters. He arrived nearly an hour after the game ended — and after quarterback Jayden Daniels met with reporters (which is very unusual, for any team).

Quinn knew all about the viral moment in which he seemed to be surprised after a failed fourth-and-two play from the San Francisco 13 in the second quarter. It looked like he didn't know it was fourth down. At the press conference, Quinn had an explanation.

" I definitely knew it was fourth down ," Quinn said, before slipping into a word salad that was largely confusing and pivoted to him explaining that they planned to go for it on fourth down throughout the game because they expected it to be a higher-scoring contest.

Even though Quinn's body language suggested that he was surprised to find out it had been fourth down, we'll give him the benefit of the doubt. He knew it was fourth down. But the operation for which he's responsible didn't know, once the penatly flag landed on the field (in plain view of quarterback Jayden Daniels) that it wasn't a situation in which failure to reach the line to gain would make it fourth and seven with a chance to kick a field goal.

When the play isn't shut down by a pre-snap foul, a penalty on the offense can be declined by the defense.

After the play, there should have been no confusion — from anyone — as to what had happened. The 49ers would decline the penalty, and the 49ers would take possession. Because it had been fourth down.

While some will believe (as I do) that Quinn (and his quarterback) didn't know it was fourth down, the explanation doesn't exonerate the lack of attention to detail. Instead, it changes the conversation from "did you know it was fourth down?" to "why didn't you realize you still had to gain at least two yards to retain possession?"

It speaks to the overall culture under Quinn. The mastery, or lack thereof, of situational football.

Quinn will get another chance to explain himself today, when he conducts his day-after press conference (unless he's fired before then). With the Commanders entering their annual bye, both Daniels and offensive coordinator David Blough won't be available to reporters until next week.

If/when there's ever an admission that a mistake was made, we know what the drill will be : "It's my responsibility. I take accountability. It won't happen again."

How many lessons will Quinn, Daniels, and Blough get to learn on the fly? Teams don't hire head coaches with the idea that there will be multiple years of on-the-job training when it comes to the nuances of the game. Quinn has been coaching in the NFL continuously since 2001, with the exception of a two-year stint at Florida in 2011 and 2012. He served as the Falcons' head coach for six years, and it's his third year with the Commanders.

In hiring Quinn, the Commanders weren't rolling the dice on a newbie. They were hiring a fully-formed football coach who presumably knows how the game works, in all respects.

The last two games have proven otherwise. And it further complicates the decision that owner Josh Harris, who is still a new, inexperienced owner, will be making as to whether to make an in-season change.

articles.title: WWE Rumors on Scary Bron Breakker Fall, R-Truth's Injury vs. Damian Priest and Ilja Dragunov in AEW
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling.

Details on Breakker's Tough Landing at Live Event

Bron Breakker avoided injury despite a scary fall from the top rope during a match at a WWE live event on Saturday night.

Teaming with fellow Vision members Bronson Reed and Austin Theory against Oba Femi, LA Knight and Penta in the main event, Breakker lost his footing on the top rope during a spot with Knight and appeared to land awkwardly on his neck:

Breakker was fortunately fine after the spot, as evidenced by the fact that he competed in a hard-hitting singles match against Penta on Monday night's episode of Raw.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t H Jenkins of Ringside News), there was "no heat" on anyone for the spot that went awry, as it was considered "a simple sort of mistake."

WrestleVotes added that people backstage in WWE decided to "no-sell" the situation rather than making it a major talking point within the company.

Given his high-impact style, Breakker does have a penchant for putting himself in harm's way at times during his matches.

At the same time, his speed, explosiveness and athleticism are what set him apart from most other Superstars, so it makes sense for him to lean into it.

Breakker was lucky to walk away from the fall with nothing significantly wrong with him, and the fact that he is already back in the ring and performing at a high level is a good sign that he should be OK moving forward.

Priest Reportedly Made Call to End Match vs. Truth

Damian Priest was reportedly the one who made the decision to end his match against R-Truth early on SmackDown last week.

According to Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t WrestlePurists ), Priest "made the call" to quickly move to the finish once he realized that Truth had gotten injured.

Alvarez praised Priest for managing to stay in character throughout the ordeal, as he never let on that he was concerned about Truth's health.

When Truth was unable to get up after executing a missile dropkick, Priest calmly spoke to the referee and went outside the ring to grab a steel chair.

That allowed Fraxiom time to run down and protect Truth from Priest, prompting Priest to leave the ring without inflicting further damage.

On Monday, Truth posted a photo of himself on X, seemingly preparing to undergo an MRI:

Truth noted in the post that he is "OK," while joking that Priest "tried to kill" him.

Priest and Truth held the WWE Tag Team Championships together from March until dropping them to The MFTs in August.

Despite that run of success, Priest turned on Truth shortly after they lost the championships, noting within the storyline that he felt Truth was holding him back.

A former world heavyweight champion, Priest is now able to portray a more serious character once again, and it could help him move back up the card in the singles ranks on SmackDown.

WWE's Reported Reaction to Dragunov Joining AEW

There are reportedly no hard feelings from anyone in WWE regarding Ilja Dragunov's decision to sign with AEW.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Jenkins ), when it comes to Dragunov, WWE wrestlers and management both "wish him well."

WrestleVotes added that there is "no animosity," and everyone who was friends with Dragunov in WWE is "happy" to see him doing what he wants to do in his career.

At the AEW WrestleDream pay-per-view on Saturday, Dragunov debuted for the company by making his entrance and eliciting a positive reaction from the live crowd.

It had been anticipated for several weeks that Dragunov was going to sign and debut with AEW following the expiration of his WWE contract.

A 33-year-old wrestler from Russia, Dragunov had been with WWE since 2019, and he enjoyed success at numerous levels.

Dragunov was the United Kingdom champion in NXT UK and the NXT champion in NXT before holding the United States Championship once on the main roster.

However, after dropping the U.S. title to Carmelo Hayes in December 2025, Dragunov's role and television time were diminished.

He last competed in the Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal in April, and he was off WWE TV for months after that until reports emerged that he was leaving the company.

Dragunov accomplished a great deal in WWE, but there is little doubt that his hard-hitting style in the ring should fit well in AEW, plus there is no shortage of potential dream matches at his disposal.

articles.title: England netball: Anna Stembridge named new Vitality Roses head coach
articles.summary: Anna Stembridge's second stint as England head coach after being in charge from 2011 to 2015; she has served as interim coach since March after Jess Thirlby's shock resignation prior to 2026 Commonwealth Games; Sky Sports pundit Tamsin Greenway and Jo Harten named on coaching staff
articles.body:
A former Wales international with 45 caps, Stembridge has had a previous stint as England head coach from 2011 to 2015, in which the side secured a historic first series win over Australia in 2013.

Having been assistant coach since September 2024, she has also served as interim head coach since March after Jess Thirlby's shock resignation four months prior to the 2026 Commonwealth Games.

In Glasgow, the Vitality Roses finished fourth after losing to Australia in the bronze medal match.

Reflecting on her appointment, Stembridge said: "It is an absolute honour to take on the role.

"When you talk about coaching ambitions, this is the ultimate one, so I feel very privileged.

"I've been lucky enough to work with this group of athletes over a number of years, and I'm really excited to have been appointed to lead them to the Netball World Cup."

Stembridge is joined by Sky Sports pundit Tamsin Greenway and Jo Harten in her coaching team through to next year's World Cup in August and September. Both enjoyed distinguished international careers with England.

Greenway is also head coach of the London Mavericks in the Netball Super League, and was previously in charge of Scotland from 2020 to 2023, while Harten is assistant coach of NSW Swifts in Australia's Super Netball League.

England Netball will work closely with both clubs to support the coaches in balancing their domestic and international duties.

articles.title: Magnus Carlsen, estrella en la MOVE Cup de Barcelona
articles.standfirst: El torneo volverá el ajedrez de élite a la Ciudad Condal 37 años después
articles.summary: El torneo volverá el ajedrez de élite a la Ciudad Condal 37 años después
articles.body: La MOVE Cup, un nuevo torneo de ajedrez de élite que traerá a Barcelona a los mejores grandes maestros del mundo, se ha presentado oficialmente este martes en una rueda de prensa en Barcelona. La Ciudad Condal volverá a tener un torneo de élite 37 años después. La MOVE Cup es una nueva competición que aspira a convertirse en na cita habitual del calendario ajedrecístico mundial y que tiene la vocación solidaria como eje central. La gran estrella de la competición será el gran maestro y número 1, Magnus Carlsen. Para encontrar la última vez que el mejor del ajedrez participó en España fue en el Mundial de Linares 2005 cuando se retiró Garri Kasparov. En las redes sociales se anunciará la venta de entradas en próximas fechas. La bolsa en premios será de 300.000 euros. "Jugué en Barcelona en 2023, pero jugando partidas por internet", recuerda Carlsen. "Tengo muchas ganas de jugar aquí en enero. Hay que organizar torneos de ajedrez atractivos para los aficionados y este será uno de ellos seguro. Queremos a los mejores jugando de una manera rápida a la vez que divertida. Para mí el ajedrez es el deporte más interesante del mundo y creo que es bueno para los niños". Carlsen toma ejemplo de los eSports para mejorar el feedback con los seguidores de la ajedrez. Sobre su ausencia en el Campeonato del Mundo, el noruega comenta que "hay cosas ahora mismo que me interesan más".
