articles.title: Tote confiesa cuánto ha llegado a pagar por una botella de vino
articles.standfirst: El exfutbolista sorprende a David Sánchez en Despierta San Francisco al hablar de su afición por el vino y revela con quién compartiría sus botellas más exclusivas
articles.summary: El exfutbolista sorprende a David Sánchez en Despierta San Francisco al hablar de su afición por el vino y revela con quién compartiría sus botellas más exclusivas
articles.body: El exfutbolista Tote ha protagonizado una divertida conversación con David Sánchez en Despierta San Francisco, de Radio MARCA, en la que ha repasado la actualidad futbolística y ha dejado algunas confesiones sobre su vida personal. Entre ellas, su pasión por el vino, una afición por la que ha llegado a desembolsar una importante cantidad de dinero. Todo ha comenzado cuando Tote ha explicado cómo tenía previsto disfrutar de la jornada de Champions desde casa: "Voy a ver dos y bueno, me abriré una botellita de vino". Una declaración que ha despertado la curiosidad de David Sánchez, que no ha dudado en preguntarle por la botella más cara que había comprado en su vida. La respuesta del exfutbolista ha sorprendido al presentador: "No, tampoco creas que mucho. Habré pagado cerca de mil euros. 800, 900 euros". Además, Tote ha aclarado que se trataba de una botella adquirida para consumir en su propia casa y no en un restaurante. Pese a reconocer que ha llegado a gastar semejante cantidad, Tote ha asegurado que no es partidario de pagar precios desorbitados por una botella: "Yo creo que el vino tiene un precio". Para el exjugador, esta afición va mucho más allá del dinero y está estrechamente relacionada con las experiencias que ha vivido a lo largo de su carrera. "El vino lo tengo mucho en recuerdos", ha explicado, antes de recordar su etapa en Valladolid: "Tengo recuerdos muy bonitos. Entonces el vino lo asemejo a esos recuerdos, ¿no? Y muchas veces compro vino de la Ribera por eso". David Sánchez también ha querido saber si una botella de semejante precio estaba reservada para una ocasión especial o para compartirla con su pareja. Sin embargo, Tote ha dejado claro que no hace distinciones cuando recibe invitados en casa: "Yo la abro con cualquiera que venga a mi casa". Y ha añadido: "Yo vengo a mi casa y le digo, entrad y coged la que queráis". Más allá de las anécdotas personales, Tote también ha analizado la actualidad futbolística. Uno de los protagonistas ha sido Lamine Yamal, al que ha elogiado después de su gol ante el Betis: "Un jugador que va a ser un jugador de época, ya lo es, pero tiene todavía un margen de crecimiento". El exfutbolista también ha destacado la evolución de Álex Baena en el Atlético de Madrid y las posibilidades del conjunto rojiblanco en las competiciones eliminatorias. "Al Atlético de Madrid este año, no sé si la Liga le va a dar, porque con un Barça de esta forma es muy complicado. Pero sí que la Copa del Rey y la Champions, en torneos que son, entre comillas, cortos, va a ser un equipo muy difícil de ganar", ha señalado.

articles.title: Anna Stembridge named England coach for 2027 World Cup
articles.summary: England have appointed Anna Stembridge as their head coach through to the 2027 Netball World Cup in Sydney.
articles.body:
England have appointed Anna Stembridge as their head coach through to the 2027 Netball World Cup in Sydney.

The 45-year-old, who took over as interim head coach in March after Jess Thirlby stepped down, failed to guide the Roses to a medal at the Commonwealth Games in August but has been given the go-ahead to continue with the team.

London Mavericks head coach Tamsin Greenway and NSW Swifts assistant Jo Harten - both England netball legends - will join Stembridge's coaching team.

Former Wales international Stembridge led the Roses to fourth place at the 2014 Commonwealth Games and a first series win over Australia in 2013 during a first spell as head coach.

She then served as an assistant coach to Thirlby from 2024.

In August, Stembridge said she would "reassess" whether she could continue as head coach, with an open recruitment process taking place.

England Netball chair Baroness Sue Campbell said Stembridge was the outstanding candidate and demonstrated "a clear sense of what is needed to take the team forward".

Stembridge said: "Building on the experience that the squad and I had at the Commonwealth Games, I'm fiercely focused on putting us in a position where we can compete for a medal at the World Cup next summer."

Next year's World Cup takes place in Sydney, Australia, from 25 August to 5 September.

England were beaten finalists at the last World Cup, in 2023, when Australia denied them in the final.

articles.title: Mark Allen: Former world number one considering retirement after Northern Ireland Open exit
articles.summary: Mark Allen says that retiring from snooker is "something I have been contemplating for a while" following his 4-2 loss to Jordan Brown in the Northern Ireland Open.
articles.body:
An emotional Mark Allen said retiring from snooker is "something I have been contemplating for a while" following his first-round loss to Jordan Brown in the Northern Ireland Open.

Allen was beaten 4-2 by fellow Antrim man Brown in his first event since losing to Wu Yize in heartbreaking fashion in the semi-finals of the World Championship in Sheffield in May.

The former world number one said showing up to play his match against Brown was an "achievement" after a "really difficult" period in his life while he took a break from competitive action.

"I think if I hadn't have been playing Jordan, I probably would not have played," Allen told BBC Sport NI after his defeat at the Waterfront Hall in Belfast.

"I felt like I did not want my last match to be remembered for that semi-final in Sheffield.

"I thought it would be a bit of nostalgia to go out playing Jordan in the Waterfront where it all started in 2005 and that would be a more fitting end if I do call it a day.

Asked if he is considering drawing the curtain on his career, he replied: "Yeah."

Allen exits NI Open with Brown loss on return

The 40-year-old has had a decorated career, winning 12 ranking tournaments including the 2022 UK Championship since he turned professional in 2005.

However, this year has been a challenging one for Allen after he missed a match-winning black in the semi-final against Yize in May during the penultimate frame that would have taken him into his first World Championship final.

Allen went on to lose the final frame against eventual champion Yize and has since been a notable absentee from the World Snooker Tour circuit.

"The last three months have been really, really difficult and I think even just being here today is an achievement," added Allen.

"For me, today was not about the result or the performance, it was trying to enjoy the experience of playing one of my best mates in one of my favourite arenas, in one of my favourite tournaments.

"I am not going to announce it [retirement] right now after a defeat but it is something I have been contemplating for a while and something needs to change within the next six weeks before the UK Championship for me to show up and I need to work hard on myself in the next few weeks and see what is around the corner."

Allen received a warm response from his home crowd as he returned to the venue where he became back-to-back champion in 2021 and 2022.

It was clear the respect that both players had for each other following the match with Allen adding he "wished Jordan well, I always do".

The world number 65 said the win was "the least satisfying" he has ever had as he progressed to the last 32 to face Michael Holt.

"It is overwhelming for Mark here with his family, friends and all the fans who have paid good money to see him play," said Brown.

"It is very difficult. I have my own battles to go through. I am in a precarious place in the rankings, and I lost my mum recently. It just puts everything into perspective.

"The general public seem to think we are just robots who just turn up to pot a few balls, it is not like that at all."

Matches between Brown and Allen have always been close contests with Tuesday's win the 39-year-old's first victory over his close friend.

"I really hope so," Brown replied when asked if he thought Allen would reconsider retiring.

"The first words I said to him today was it was great to see him back and we had a big cuddle. It is tough to see him going through that.

"I have no doubt he will come back. Snooker is his love, he is absolutely brilliant and the game and he is a top bloke, I wish him all the best."

articles.title: El futbolista del Atlético en el que se ve reflejado Adelardo
articles.standfirst: La leyenda del Atlético de Madrid se deshace en elogios hacia uno de los pupilos de Simeone en El Programa de Ortega y analiza las aspiraciones del equipo
articles.summary: La leyenda del Atlético de Madrid se deshace en elogios hacia uno de los pupilos de Simeone en El Programa de Ortega y analiza las aspiraciones del equipo
articles.body: Adelardo Rodríguez, una de las grandes leyendas del Atlético de Madrid, ha pasado por los micrófonos de El Programa de Ortega, de Radio MARCA, para conversar con Vicente Ortega y José Rodríguez sobre la actualidad rojiblanca y recordar algunos de los momentos más importantes de su carrera. A sus 87 años, el histórico futbolista ha tenido palabras de elogio para Pablo Barrios, un jugador en el que reconoce muchas de las cualidades que él mismo tenía cuando comenzaba su trayectoria. Adelardo ha tenido palabras de elogio a Pablo Barrios. "Es un jugador al que yo lo seguí cuando estaba en el segundo equipo, como jugaba allí al lado de casa, pues lo seguía todos los partidos", ha explicado el exfutbolista, antes de reconocer las similitudes que encuentra entre ambos: "Me recordaba a mí, cuando estaba en esa división, porque cuando jugaba a la pelota, él, su fin era hacer gol". Adelardo también ha destacado la vocación ofensiva del canterano: "Yo quería hacer gol y este chico es muy buen jugador y se mete mucho con los delanteros". Además, ha lamentado los problemas físicos que ha sufrido Barrios, aunque se ha mostrado esperanzado con su regreso: "Es una pena que haya estado lesionado, pero bueno, ya está bien y parece que va a coger su puesto". Más allá de su admiración por Pablo Barrios, la leyenda rojiblanca también ha valorado las posibilidades del Atlético de Madrid esta temporada. Adelardo confía en que los nuevos fichajes terminen de adaptarse y permitan al equipo dar un salto de calidad. "Hay jugadores que ya saben lo que tienen que hacer, hay otros que a lo mejor todavía le va a costar un poco más, pero creo que los fichajes del equipo son buenos y el equipo creo que va a subir este año bastante", ha señalado. Sin embargo, el exfutbolista considera que el Atlético tiene un gran obstáculo en su lucha por los títulos: el Barcelona. "Este equipo va a querer llegar al primer puesto, eso está claro. Lo que pasa es que este año nos encontramos con un equipo que no tiene rival, que es el Barça", ha afirmado. También ha tenido palabras para Julián Álvarez, del que espera una mejoría en su rendimiento: "Va a tener un año muy difícil, pero es un buen jugador y en cuanto que empiece a meter goles a la gente ya se está con él, está claro". La entrevista también ha servido para recordar la trayectoria de Adelardo y su profunda vinculación con el Atlético de Madrid. El histórico futbolista, que acaba de cumplir 87 años, ha dejado una de las frases más emotivas de la conversación: "A mí no me llaman Adelardo, me llaman Atlético de Madrid. Y eso para mí es un orgullo". El exjugador ha recordado sus primeros pasos en el club, cuando llegó a Madrid con apenas 18 años, y el papel que tuvieron sus compañeros en su adaptación: "Yo había llegado a Madrid con 18 años y no me lo creía. Entonces gracias a Joaquín Peiró, gracias a Collar, gracias a Chuzo, pues yo fui entrando en un equipo".

articles.title: Former LSU football linebacker dismissed from Auburn
articles.summary: Former LSU football linebacker Xavier Atkins was dismissed from Auburn on Monday. He plans to enter the portal again.
articles.body:
A former LSU football linebacker will be looking for a new team again as Auburn dismissed Xavier Atkins on Monday night. ESPN's Pete Thamel reported Atkins' dismissal.

Atkins' removal came less than a week after Auburn head coach Alex Golesh said Atkins was suspended for the Georgia game and wouldn't travel with the team. Auburn went on to knock off Georgia without Atkins.

Golesh was asked about Atkins at his Monday press conference and didn't say much. Golesh said the team would handle the issue in-house. The specific reasons for Atkins' dismissal are unknown, and Auburn has not released an official statement.

Atkins released a statement on social media and said, "I have nothing but respect for Auburn University and will continue to support my teammates this season. My focus is on my health, my family, and on finishing up the academic semester strong, and I'll be entering the transfer portal at the appropriate time."

Atkins had a breakout season with Auburn in 2025, earning All-SEC honors and leading the SEC in tackles for loss. Atkins was having a productive 2026 before his suspension, too.

Atkins signed with LSU in 2024 and spent one year with the Tigers before entering the transfer portal. Atkins, a four-star from Louisiana, appeared in seven games with LSU and was not a big factor in the Tigers' linebacker rotation.

LSU will face Auburn this Saturday at 11 A.M. CT.

articles.title: Christian Horner Admits Red Bull Pressured Michael Masi During 2021 F1 Finale
articles.summary: Christian Horner relays the pressure and controversial step by Michael Masi in the 2021 F1 season, as he was impressed by Hamilton’s response. There is no do...
articles.body:
Christian Horner relays the pressure and controversial step by Michael Masi in the 2021 F1 season, as he was impressed by Hamilton's response.

There is no doubt that the 2021 F1 season, especially the finale at the Abu Dhabi GP, will remain one of the most controversial moments in the modern history of the sport. Apart from the spygate or the crashgate, not much mind-boggling happened in the sport.

But how the finale panned out in the 2021 F1 season will be talked about forever. At the center of it were Red Bull, Max Verstappen and Horner fighting Mercedes, Hamilton and Toto Wolff. The ultimate villain ended up being the then FIA Race Director Masi.

Throughout the 2021 F1 season, Verstappen and Hamilton were at it; whether it was the incident at Silverstone or Monza or even Saudi Arabia, they were at the flashpoint always. Naturally, for it to come down to the finale, tied on points? Scripted, everyone would say.

Mercedes Came Up with Lawyers Just in Case

"Why didn't I have any Grey hairs before that race? That season had been epic from the very first race in Bahrain, where the two drivers had gone head-to-head," said Horner on the Up to Speed podcast . "We just lost out. Lewis and Max must have rubbed wheels pretty much every Grand Prix.

"It was kind of like a heavyweight bout that we came to this final round that you couldn't have scripted it off the back of Saudi Arabia, where there'd been a brake test and a load of drama there. One week later, we're in Abu Dhabi, and the drivers are tied on points, but Max is ahead on race wins. So, if they do a Senna-Prost at the first corner, Max is the world champion. I'm sure that in Mercedes' mind, they thought they had crashed all year. That's going to be their tactic.

"So, they came lawyered-up or barristered up to the race, ready to take on that action if it were to happen," summed up Horner, who then explained how the race weekend shaped up with Verstappen on pole using an extra set, with Hamilton on the front row.

The role of Sergio Perez was important too, as his 'Minister of Defence' moment certainly helped Verstappen and Red Bull during the race. But the Grand Prix already started with a banger moment, when the Brit took run-off at the Turn 6-7 sequence.

Of course, Red Bull hustled for a penalty, but the FIA brushed it off. Horner recalled how they had a direct line to speak with Masi, which had been in place for a few years, unlike the time under Charlie Whiting, who always spoke with Team Managers or Sporting Directors on any matter related to the race.

"We go into race day, Sergio comes to see me in the morning," continued Horner. "What do you want me to do today? And I said, look, just do whatever you can to help your teammate. He said, 'look, pay me my bonus, I'll do whatever you like', that was the thing with Checo. He was very easy to deal with.

"And I said, look, 'whatever you can do to strategically, if it comes into play'. And sure enough, Lewis got the better start. He got off the line better. Max had a rundown on him down to the first chicane, Lewis went in deep. He outbraked himself, so we're immediately…at that point, you were able to have a direct line to Michael Masi, which I hadn't realized had been going on for the last few years until Barcelona of that year where we'd said that everything should be broadcast at a previous Formula 1 Commission meeting.

"And then I'm hearing Toto on the line to Michael telling him what he shouldn't be doing. Now when Charlie Whiting [former FIA Race Director], I never spoke to Charlie directly in 20 years or whatever it was. And so, now we've got a situation where a team principal is actively putting pressure on the rate on the referee, which is a huge power tool. Well, step this up a gear, Jonathan [Wheatley], warm me up. It then starts ratcheting through the season at Silverstone and whatever else.

"So, we get to that chicane, Lewis has gone in deep, hasn't given the place back. We're on to Michael, 'Michael, come on. This is, he's taken too much of an advantage here. Max was so going to make that pass. He's got to give the place back'. Lewis smartly eased off, let the gap open up in sector three of the track. Of course, you're not going to be able to pass. And it was okay; nothing's going our way.

"In all honesty, that day Lewis had better race pace than us. He was pulling away; Max is gradually dropping back. He couldn't hang on," summed up Horner, who was waiting for a miracle, even after trying all, from a two-stop to Perez's epic Defence. It arrived eventually during the closing stages when Williams' Nicholas Latifi crashed in the final part of the circuit, resulting in the safety car deployment.

This was the moment that turned things around. With only a handful of laps remaining, it looked like they may not get to get a green lap. Horner and Red Bull were urging Masi to get going. Initially, the Australian resisted but then used his discretion to unlap the cars. The Brit said it was all okay what he did until the decision to unlap only a handful of cars.

Horner agrees that allowing only cars between Hamilton and Verstappen to unlap was controversial and not the right move, but he clarified that Red Bull only pressured Masi to get on with the race, not directed him to unlap only a handful of cars. "Nicholas Latifi did his thing, and it didn't look like a massive accident," continued Horner. "There was a crane and an exit point pretty close by.

Red Bull Pressured but Masi Committed the Grave Mistake

"So, it looked like they were going to tidy it pretty quickly. They're back out [after pit stop], but there's the lapped cars between Max and Lewis which would have taken, by the time he'd have got through them, Lewis would have been down those two straights, and it would have been done. So, it was like, 'come on, Michael, there's more than enough time', which there was. 'Let them on that', now, the only controversial thing that he did, he let the cars…originally said no, the cars are not to unlap and then by putting pressure on him, he agreed to unlap the cars between Max and Lewis.

"It was fine to let them all unlap; within his rule book, he can do that. He had the right to do that, hadn't done it previously. And so, if he'd have gone back, I'm sure he would have just said all of them to unlap because that was the only controversial thing. It was no fault of ours. So, at that point, Max is then on a fresh set of softs," summed up Horner.

With no cars in between and Verstappen on fresher tires, the Dutchman was able to make the move on Hamilton, who resisted and almost came back on him. But the Red Bull had enough by the end to see the checkered flag and claim his first F1 drivers' title in an epic finale – which unfortunately would be known for different reasons.

What impressed Horner was the humility shown not just by Hamilton, but also by his father, Anthony, who had the capacity to congratulate Red Bull and Verstappen, despite all that transpired in the last 30 minutes. They were not as composed in the stewards' room, but right at that moment, the Brit was left impressed.

"I think I mentioned it in my book, because well, I was super impressed," recalled Horner. "I mean his world has fallen apart and he had the charisma within him to acknowledge and congratulate Max, to congratulate me, and stand up there on that podium must have been immensely, immensely hard for him in that moment.

"And I have to say his father as well, afterwards, congratulated myself, members of the team. And then all hell let loose in the stewards' office afterwards. But yeah, it was…really I mean you could not have scripted that finish," summed up Horner.

articles.title: Hawkeyes Look to Keep Rolling at Minnesota
articles.summary: Iowa rolls into Minneapolis looking to keep their momentum going after the bye week.
articles.body:
The bye week is over, the pig is packed for a road trip and the "OR" is back.

The Hawkeyes have taken a week of additional rest and practice but the question of who will be under center is back in the fore after Jeremy Hecklinski led Iowa to their first win west of the Rockies in a generation and Hank Brown continues to work back from his shoulder injury.

One of them will lead Iowa on the road for a second straight game as the #15 Hawkeyes head to Minneapolis to take on the 4-2 Minnesota Golden Gophers. It's Minnesota's homecoming, both teams are coming off byes and the winner gets to keep climbing in a Big Ten race that got messier while Iowa rested.

The Hawkeyes opened as 4.5-point favorites in this one according to FanDuel Sportsbook . That number has climbed to Iowa -6.5 with an over/under of 41.5 total points. That pencils out to an implied final somewhere around 24-17 Iowa. For a road trophy game against a team that has been solid much of the year, that's a statement about how these two teams are trending.

The Hawkeyes come in off their best power four performance of the season, having thoroughly dominated the Huskies at Washington. It was the first power conference opponent where Iowa topped 300 yards or 21 points all season and they did both in a single game. That helped the P4 averages up to 318 yards and 22.75 points per game. Both of those feel like winning numbers in Minneapolis.

Figuring out the Gophers requires accepting two facts at once. Minnesota beat both ranked teams they've played – 27-24 at Washington and 20-14 over Michigan for the Little Brown Jug. But both those teams are now unranked and they also got run out of their own building by Mississippi State 38-13 and thumped 41-13 at Purdue ahead of the bye.

Drake Lindsey has been a competent trigger man completing 64.8% of his passes for 1,335 yards with 9 touchdowns, but the picks are piling up (he's got five on the season). Iowa will surely look to add to that turnover number on Saturday and set up the offense for some short fields. Javon Tracy (yes, that is the younger brother of former Hawkeye and Boilermaker Tyrone Tracy) is the main target at 32 catches for 375 yards and a score. The Gopher defense has real pieces in Maverick Baranowski (team-high 45 tackles) and TJ Bush Jr. (4 sacks).

Minnesota's rushing offense ranks 129th in the country at 104.8 yards a game. It's running into Iowa's rush defense, which ranks 7th at 84.7 yards per game allowed and just held Washington to-3 yards on the ground. If that holds to form, Lindsey ends up throwing 35-plus times into a defense allowing 14.5 points a game, a pass rush that has 19 sacks and a secondary that is looking to earn their place among the ball Hawks.

On the other side, the key is simpler still. Minnesota's run defense is respectable (52nd) and its scoring defense middling (T-54th at 21.8). Iowa just hung 41 on the road with a balanced attack, but can they keep that momentum going in the run game to avoid becoming one-dimensional? Feed Moulton, stay out of third-and-long, don't gift the homecoming crowd a short field. Iowa's formula doesn't need to change in Minneapolis. It just needs to show up for four quarters.

Here's a quick look at the details for Saturday.

Date: Saturday, October 24th Time: 2:30 pm CT Matchup: #15 Iowa Hawkeyes (5-1, 2-1) at Minnesota Golden Gophers (4-2, 2-1) Location: Huntington Bank Stadium – Minneapolis, Minnesota TV: FS1 Updated Weather Forecast: Cloudy with temps in the upper 60s, 40% chance of rain in the afternoon FanDuel Opening Line : Iowa -4.5, O/U 40.5

Minnesota leads the all-time series 63-54-2 across 119 meetings dating back to 1891. But the trophy era says Iowa, 46-43-2 since 1935 – the year Iowa governor Clyde Herring and Minnesota governor Floyd Olson bet a live hog on the game. Minnesota won, Herring paid up with a pig named Floyd and the bronze version has been the best trophy in college football ever since.

Lately it's been a one-way relationship. Iowa won eight straight from 2015 to 2022, dropped the 12-10 "not a fair catch" game in 2023 – still Fleck's only win against Ferentz – then took it right back with 31-14 in Minneapolis in 2024 with the 41-3 demolition in Iowa City last year. Iowa has won 10 of the last 11 in the series and five straight trips to Huntington Bank Stadium. The Gophers haven't beaten Iowa at home in more than a decade.

For Iowa, this is step one of the six-game march we mapped out during the bye : win out, and the playoff resume takes care of itself. Nobody hands out credit for near-misses.

For Minnesota, the season funnels into this stretch. A homecoming upset of #15 Iowa would relaunch the Gophers' season. A loss makes it three defeats in four games with Indiana and UCLA still looming.

My take: the version of Minnesota that showed up against Michigan can absolutely win this game, but that version hasn't shown up in back-to-back weeks all season and Iowa certainly seems to be trending in the right direction on offense with a defense that is as solid as ever.

articles.title: Allen considers retirement after NI Open exit
articles.summary: Mark Allen says that retiring from snooker is "something I have been contemplating for a while" following his 4-2 loss to Jordan Brown in the Northern Irelan...
articles.body:
An emotional Mark Allen said retiring from snooker is "something I have been contemplating for a while" following his first-round loss to Jordan Brown in the Northern Ireland Open.

Allen was beaten 4-2 by fellow Antrim man Brown in his first event since losing to Wu Yize in heartbreaking fashion during the semi-finals of the World Championship in Sheffield in May.

The former world number one said showing up to play his match against Brown was an "achievement" after a "really difficult" period in his life while he took a break from competitive action.

"I think if I hadn't have been playing Jordan, I probably would not have played," Allen told BBC Sport NI after his defeat at the Waterfront Hall in Belfast.

"I felt like I did not want my last match to be remembered for that semi-final in Sheffield.

"I thought it would be a bit of nostalgia to go out playing Jordan in the Waterfront where it all started in 2005 and that would be a more fitting end if I do call it a day."

Asked if he is considering drawing the curtain on his career, he replied: "Yeah."

The 40-year-old has had a decorated career, winning 12 ranking tournaments including the 2022 UK Championship since he turned professional in 2005.

This year has been a challenging one for Allen, after he missed a match-winning black in the semi-final against Wu in May during the penultimate frame that would have taken him into his first World Championship final.

Allen went on to lose the final frame against eventual champion Wu and has since been a notable absentee from the World Snooker Tour circuit.

"The last three months have been really, really difficult and I think even just being here today is an achievement," added Allen.

"For me, today was not about the result or the performance, it was trying to enjoy the experience of playing one of my best mates in one of my favourite arenas, in one of my favourite tournaments.

"I am not going to announce it [retirement] right now after a defeat but it is something I have been contemplating for a while and something needs to change within the next six weeks before the UK Championship for me to show up and I need to work hard on myself in the next few weeks and see what is around the corner."

Allen received a warm response from his home crowd as he returned to the venue where he became back-to-back champion in 2021 and 2022.

It was clear the respect that both players had for each other following the match with Allen adding he "wished Jordan well, I always do".

The world number 65 said the win was "the least satisfying" he has ever had as he progressed to the last 32 to face Michael Holt.

"It is overwhelming for Mark here with his family, friends and all the fans who have paid good money to see him play," said Brown.

"It is very difficult. I have my own battles to go through. I am in a precarious place in the rankings, and I lost my mum recently. It just puts everything into perspective.

"The general public seem to think we are just robots who just turn up to pot a few balls, it is not like that at all."

Matches between Brown and Allen have always been close contests, with Tuesday's win the 39-year-old's first victory over his close friend.

"I really hope so," Brown replied when asked if he thought Allen would reconsider retiring.

"The first words I said to him today was it was great to see him back and we had a big cuddle. It is tough to see him going through that.

"I have no doubt he will come back. Snooker is his love, he is absolutely brilliant and he is a top bloke, I wish him all the best."

articles.title: ‘Praying for Terry’: Jayden Daniels Reacts to Commanders WR’s Major Knee Scare
articles.summary: Washington Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin left Monday night’s 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on a cart with a left knee injury the team fears...
articles.body:
Washington Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin left Monday night's 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on a cart with a left knee injury the team fears is serious. He went down without contact in the first quarter at Levi's Stadium, and the Commanders ruled him out right away.

Quarterback Jayden Daniels addressed the injury after the game and spoke about McLaurin in personal terms while the 1-4-1 Commanders await an official diagnosis.

Jayden Daniels reacts to Terry McLaurin's knee injury in Commanders' loss to 49ers

McLaurin's left knee buckled as he cut to the outside on third-and-9 with 2:16 left in the first quarter. He stayed down while teammates knelt nearby, and trainers took him off on a cart with his leg in an air cast. Cornerback Deommodore Lenoir was in coverage on the route. McLaurin caught one pass for 27 yards on the opening drive, which ended in a field goal. He played seven snaps.

Quarterback Jayden Daniels, McLaurin's teammate since 2024, addressed the devastating injury after the game.

He said , "He's a brother to me. It sucks. You see how hard he works … Praying for Terry," Daniels said, noting that McLaurin has been right by his side through adversity, adding, "I love Terry and appreciate him a lot."

Head coach Dan Quinn addressed the injury postgame, noting that full scan results would provide clarity. "The concern is that it could be significant. We'll do the scans tomorrow and give you an update when I visit with you guys," Quinn said .

Former NFL team doctor David J. Chao reviewed video of the play. Though he has not examined McLaurin, Chao shared his concern on X, penning , "By video, worry for left patella tendon rupture. Leg just gives out. Horrible. Would mean surgery and season. Carted off with airsplint."

The team awaits Tuesday's scan results to determine the exact severity. To navigate McLaurin's absence, Stefon Diggs will step up to fill the primary WR1 role for Washington, while Dyami Brown and Luke McCaffrey are expected to see increased targets on the perimeter.

Losing McLaurin hurts the offense. The 31-year-old has 15 catches for 230 yards and a touchdown in five games this season and he already missed Week 4 with a hamstring injury. This scenario mirrors the team's brutal 2025 season, which fell apart after Daniels missed critical time with severe knee and hamstring issues while McLaurin was simultaneously sidelined by a major quad tear, ultimately forcing Washington into a disappointing 5-12 finish.

articles.title: FIA boss reveals firm stance on staging of Abu Dhabi and Qatar F1 races
articles.summary: The final two races of the 2026 campaign are set to go ahead despite conflict in the Middle East
articles.body:
FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem insists the final two races of the Formula 1 season in Qatar (29 November) and Abu Dhabi (6 December) will take place as planned.

Grand prix events in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia in April were cancelled due to the US-Iran war and subsequent conflict in the Middle East. Over the summer, F1 revealed a mid-September deadline for making a call on the final two rounds, with Imola in Italy acting as a one-off back-up option for the first weekend in December.

That deadline then extended to mid-October, with F1 now telling personnel to move ahead as planned unless told otherwise. That being said, grandstands are being built at Imola in case of a change of circumstances.

In recent weeks, two container ships were sunk near the Strait of Hormuz after being struck by missiles while, separately, sites in Saudi Arabia have been targeted by the Yemeni separatist group the Houthis, with 13 people killed at Riyadh Airport.

As such, Emirati executive Ben Sulayem was asked whether Qatar and Abu Dhabi were "fine" to stage Formula 1 races. As reported by The Race , he replied: "Yeah, fine. One thing I would say: I have my children there [in the UAE]. You think I would leave them there and I'm here now with you [if it was dangerous]?

"You have to be sensible in this. Saying: 'Are we going to have an issue?' is one thing. But what you read in the media is actually different than what we have there.

"What we read and see on TV, we say, 'Where is it?' We don't have that, really. Otherwise why would I stay there? Why would I leave my family there?

"Does this say that there is nothing that is going to happen? I can't predict this. I can only tell you today that there is nothing and the two races are going to happen."

articles.title: Penguins 10-game progress report: Observations and trends from the start of the season
articles.summary: Checking in with the Pittsburgh Penguins in 10-game segments.
articles.body:
As much as we try, it can be tough to get a read on a team, good or bad, after the first handful of games to a season. You probably need to see at least 20 or 25 games before you start to get a true sense for how good or bad a team really is. But breaking a season down into 10-game segments can be a pretty good barometer for how a team is playing during a certain stretch, and if any trends (good or bad) are starting to emerge.

After the first 10 games you can at least start to pick out some thing that are either encouraging or a warning sign.

With the 2026-27 Penguins, there are a lot of warning signs.

So much so, that if things do not start to trend in a different direction very soon it might be time to start asking if this is the year things really do bottom out for them.

We will do a progress report after every 10-game stretch to see where the team is, and how it is progressing.

This is the first of those progress reports.

Ten-game record: 3-6-1 (7 points, 14th in Eastern Conference, 27th in NHL)

Goal differential: minus-5 (24th in NHL)

Goals against per game: 3.70 (27th in NHL)

Penalty kill: 80.8 percent (15th in NHL)

Expected Goals For Per 60 minutes (5-on-5): 3.o7 (6th in NHL)

Expected Goals Against Per 60 minutes (5-on-5): 2.53 (17th in NHL)

Expected Goals Share (5-on-5): 54.8 percent (7th in NHL)

All-Situations Save Percentage: .867 (25th in NHL)

Goals Saved Above Expected (all situations): minus-2.5

There is an argument to be made the Penguins have been a little unlucky offensively, at least based on the number of chances they've generated. And honestly, I think that passes the eye test as well. The offensive slump after the first two games largely comes down to 1) the power play being a mess until Monday's game in Utah, and 2) not enough finishing.

I still believe in the offense, and I really haven't seen anything to suggest it can't still be a good offensive team. There is enough forward talent there to score goals and I have to imagine some of these guys (looking at you, Rickard Rakell) are going to find the net eventually.

The bigger problem, as we should have probably feared, is everything regarding this team's play defensively.

The biggest wild-card with them was always going to be what the goalies do. Arturs Silovs and Sergei Murashov were either going to do enough to cover up their defensive flaws and help them get to the playoffs, or they were going to struggle behind a sub-par defense and help send them to the lottery.

While I'm not going to put all of the goals against numbers on them, I don't think it's unfair to say that they haven't consistently bailed them out (Sergei Murashov's game in Columbus being the obvious exception to that).

Don't take that as too much of a criticism. Because it's not meant to be.

There is only so much a goalie can do, and there's only so much expectation you can have for duo that includes a rookie goalie as one half of it, and a guy that probably projects as more of a backup than a starter as the other half of it. It's just simply a statement of fact: That was one of the wild-card things that needed to go their way, and so far, it is has not played out that way.

The bigger issue is everything else regarding the team defensively, and it's something everybody has to own.

The thing about the defensive struggles that are especially maddening is it's not always a constant problem.

In terms of VOLUME, the chances against are not anything outrageous. It's not great, but it's not as bad as it could be, or as bad as some other teams in the NHL.

The problem is that when the mistakes and breakdowns DO happen, they are cataclysmic. Like, complete, system-wide break downs involving everybody on the ice that just shouldn't be happening.

When they screw up, they get their money's worth out of it.

I admit, I kind of liked this defense on paper, at least compared to last year's group, but the early returns so far have not been good. They don't exit the zone well, they don't defend zone entries well, and they spend too much time chasing the puck in their own zone. It is a disruption to everything in all three zones. Add in some poor support from the forwards and you've got a team that has allowed way too many goals, in way too few games.

1. You might not be able to clinch a playoff spot in October, but you can play your way out of it. The Penguins gave themselves a cushion early in the 2025-26 season by banking a lot of early points and starting off 7-2-1 through 10 games.

They are doing the opposite this season and putting themselves into an early season hole that, historically, is tough to climb out of.

In the salary cap era there have been 112 teams that won three games or less over the first 10 games of a season.

Only six teams have done it since the start of the 2016-17 season.

Only two have done it since the start of the 2021-22 season: The 2025-26 Minnesota Wild (3-5-2) and the 2023-24 Edmonton Oilers (2-7-1).

So … that is what you are looking at here.

2. Perhaps the most eye-opening part of this 10-game stretch is that the Penguins played three straight games against legitimate contenders in Colorado, Vegas and Utah and were outscored 16-8 in those games. There's a bit of a gap here, obviously.

3. Along those lines, if you are in the group of fans that thinks the Penguins might need to bottom out for a year and get a top pick, you might get your wish this season. At least as long as the defensive effort and goaltending keeps doing what they have over the first 10 games. There's still 74 games remaining. There's a lot of time for things to change. They've played a pretty tough schedule so far with a lot of travel, while also having a lot of new faces thrown in together. It was never going to be perfect. But should it be as bad as it has been?

4. While nobody has been consistently good over the first 10 games the players that have stood out the most and impressed me the most have been Ben Kindel, Nicholas Robertson, the fourth line as a whole, and Sam Girard.

5. I really do not understand the Robertson usage. He is a younger player, he brings an element of speed to the lineup that a lot of the team is lacking, he is generating chances (and goals) at a rate higher than almost every other player on the team, always brings energy, and every line he has played on has been better with him on it than when he is off of it. Not only is he a guy you should want to find out about, he is also simply one of their most effective players right now.

6. I know Kindel is on a six-game point drought, but I still like his game. There needs to be reasonable expectations for 19-year-olds. Young players will struggle at times. If you want guys like him, Murashov, Ville Koivunen and whoever else is in Wilkes-Barre/Scranton to get opportunities and bring some youth into the lineup, you have to be prepared for what youth sometimes does. Sometimes it struggles. Sometimes the production is not there. Part of the process.

7. Erik Karlsson's offense is still a major factor, but I feel like he's played into a lot of the puck management and defensive coverage issues that have plagued the team.

8. No forward line has been more damaging to the team's defensive efforts than the top line. It's a problem

The Penguins have had six forward line combinations play at least 25 minutes together this season.

Crosby-Rust-Rakell is the only one that is underwater in terms of expected goal share while they are fourth in actual goal-differential. In terms of goals against per 60 minutes, they are fifth. Given the number of minutes they play (literally the most minutes) they are a shocking drain defensively. What makes it even more concerning is they are getting heavy offensive zone starts and they are still ending up moving in the wrong direction.

When none of those three players are on the ice the Penguins are actually outscoring their opponents during 5-on-5 play (it is only 13-12, but still…) with a significantly better expected goal share.

If the team is going to win games this season, that can not happen. They need more, and better, from that trio. No other way to put it.

9. The only defense pairings that have even come close to being functional and produced anything close to passable results are Girard and Kaedan Korczak, and the little bit we have seen from Kris Letang and Spencer Stastney.

10. I had reasonably high hopes for Declan Carlile, and while it's too soon to give up on him (I am not), he has been a serious issue the past few games, even with the occasional goal.

articles.title: Who are Cincinnati's undefeated football teams entering Week 10?
articles.summary: With one more regular-season game left in Ohio and two in Kentucky, who are Cincinnati's remaining undefeated high school football teams?
articles.body:
Entering Week 8 of the high school football season, nine teams in Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky were undefeated and playing for perfect records. In the two weeks since , Cincinnati College Preparatory Academy, Dayton, Deer Park, Goshen, and Hughes have taken losses, leaving only four undefeated Cincinnati-area teams

Three of the remaining undefeated squads come from Ohio and have just one more regular season game left to win for a flawless regular season. One comes from Northern Kentucky with two more regular-season games to play.

See the remaining four undefeated locals below with some facts on their current and past regular-season successes.

In eight games played, Beechwood has allowed more than a touchdown just once. The Tigers are 8-0 with their 42-35 win against Covington Catholic the only game to finish within a score. The next closest game was their 41-3 win over Dixie Heights.

In the last two weeks, the Tigers beat St. Henry 62-0 and Gallatin County 69-0 to make their point differential 423-45. Take away the CovCath contest and it is a 381-10 advantage.

From 2021 to this season, the Tigers have gone 54-4 in the regular season, losing only to Covington Catholic once each season from 2022 to 2025. Those four regular-season losses since 2021 go against three Class 2A state championships in the same span.

Remaining schedule: Oct. 23 at Bracken County (2-6), Oct. 30 at Campbell County (3-5)

RPI standings: 0.75423 (3rd in Class 2A)

The Trojans have continued to dominate every team on their schedule despite having to address some eligibility issues in court .

In the last two weeks, North College Hill notched its sixth and seventh shutouts of the year with victories against Clark Montessori and Cincinnati Country Day. The 62-0 and 70-0 wins bumped the Trojans' point differential this season to 432-3. A field goal from the 43-3 win at Summit Country Day remains the lone points allowed by the Trojans this year.

North College Hill finishes the regular season at Norwood. The Indians are 1-8 this year and have been shut out four times, including the last two weeks.

The Trojans were denied a possible 10-0 regular season with their Week 1 game against Fairport Harding canceled. The Skippers are 1-7 this year and have been shut out four times, not including a Week 3 forfeit.

Remaining schedule: Oct. 23 at Norwood (1-8)

Playoff point standings: 18.6420 points (3rd in Region 16)

The Vikings have already clinched a share of the Greater Miami Conference title , winning the conference for the fourth-straight year (including a split with Lakota West in 2024).

Princeton has outscored teams 385-103 this year and has allowed just seven or fewer points in six of its nine wins.

Michigan commit Monsanna Torbert hasn't played at quarterback in the last four weeks, but the Vikings have rolled with Key'Sean Torbert taking over the role and Jordan Hall continuing to have success running the ball.

Remaining schedule: Oct. 23 vs. Fairfield (5-4)

Playoff point standings: 30.2500 (1st in Region 4)

Deer Park lost to Indian Hill in 42-22 Week 9, preventing a regular-season finale against Wyoming with perfect regular seasons on the line.

Wyoming, with a win, would be 10-0 for the second time in three seasons. The Cowboys haven't lost a regular-season game to a team not named Indian Hill since a 28-20 loss at Reading in Week 9 of the 2015 season. Since that loss, Wyoming has gone 104-2 in the regular season, with losses to Indian Hill in 2023 and 2025.

Remaining schedule: Oct. 23 at Deer Park (8-1)

Playoff point standings: 22.2677 (1st in Region 16)

articles.title: Yankees Reportedly Reach Decision On Aaron Boone's Future
articles.summary: The New York Yankees are bringing back Aaron Boone as their manager next season
articles.body:
According to NorthJersey.com's Pete Caldera , the New York Yankees are bringing Aaron Boone back as their manager next season.

"Per an MLB executive source, Boone is returning in 2027, the final guaranteed year on his contract - an outcome that was widely anticipated," Caldera wrote on Monday.

The Yankees were embarrassingly swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Championship Series, and after the loss, Boone refused to comment on his job security. However, it was always unlikely the Yankees would move on. He will have to earn the right to come back after next season though.

Boone has been to one World Series in his time as the Yankees manager and has gone to the postseason in all but one of his nine seasons as manager. However, the expectations of being the manager of the Yankees are higher than those of other franchises.

He is being asked to deliver a championship, and the front office is one of the most aggressive in baseball. He has all the resources to win, and it's not a great look when two teams without the same resources are playing in this year's Fall Classic.

Boone has a 790-565 regular season record, but is 27-30 in the postseason. He did help lead the Yankees to an American League pennant in 2024, but fans are well within their rights to be frustrated.

Every year, it seems like the same problems plague the Yankees, and at some point it falls on the manager to fix them. The Yankees have Aaron Judge, who is one of the best hitters ever, and have failed to win it all. It's fair for fans to wonder if someone else could actually get the job done with their talented roster.

articles.title: Week 7 Top Overall Fantasy Football Waiver Wire Targets: Terrance Ferguson, Ja'Kobi Lane, And More Top Options
articles.summary: The top overall fantasy football waiver wire pickups for every position in Week 7.
articles.body:
It's time to put Week 6 behind us and turn our attention to this week. That starts with the waiver wire. These are our top overall waiver targets for every position in Week 7.

After an impressive 2024 season, Mayfield has really fallen off a cliff. Things fell apart after the first month in 2025, and this season has not been much better. Through three games, he has thrown for 615 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions.

Still, Mayfield is just 31 years old and competent at worst. We have seen him be elite, and we are less than two years removed from him throwing for 4,500 yards and 41 touchdowns. He could get back to that level if he's finally fully healthy.

In Week 7, Tampa Bay will play the Carolina Panthers. The Panthers are allowing the 12th-most fantasy points to quarterbacks this season. Just be sure to monitor Mayfield's availability throughout the week. He's expected to play but is not a guarantee.

In Week 6, Miller was the first clear-cut RB1 in any week in New Orleans this season. He played on 44% of the offensive snaps, which led the position, and dominated the rushing volume with 20 carries. Alvin Kamara carried the ball just seven times and CJ Donaldson six. Kamara did lead the backfield with six targets, but Miller was still targeted twice. He turned his 22 opportunities into 70 yards.

We expect Miller to dominate the volume this week against the Pittsburgh Steelers. However, Etienne is eligible to return from IR in Week 8, and we don't know how things will play out after that. Nevertheless, he's a great option if you need a starter this week.

Lane returned from IR in Week 6 and played well. Even with backup quarterback Tyler Huntley struggling and only throwing for 165 yards. Things should only get better for Lane moving forward.

Baltimore is expected to get Lamar Jackson back next week, and Rashod Bateman exited Week 6 with a shoulder injury. Lane caught four of his five targets for 40 yards in Week 6, and we expect him to separate himself as the clear second option for the Ravens. He's an interesting option this week in a tough matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals, as long as Jackson plays.

Ferguson is a player you'll have to stash because he's not eligible to return from injured reserve until Week 8, but he becomes a very interesting option beyond that. Davante Adams is set to miss up to 10 weeks and could be out for the remainder of the fantasy football season. That will open the door for Ferguson to have a major role once he returns, particularly in the red zone.

We saw him get a prominent role in one game with Puka Nacua out before getting injured, and he caught six of nine targets for 54 yards and a touchdown. He has league-winning upside and should be a priority on the waiver wire.

articles.title: Kentucky extends volleyball coach Craig Skinner through 2031
articles.summary: Kentucky volleyball head coach Craig Skinner had agreed to an extension through 2031. He led the Wildcats to a national championship in 2020.
articles.body:
Kentucky volleyball head coach Craig Skinner has agreed to a contract extension through 2031, UK Athletic Director J Batt announced on Oct. 20.

Financial terms were not disclosed, but his base salary is $525,000 this season. His previous contract was signed in 2022 and effective through June of 2029. Skinner's latest extension comes after securing career win No. 500 earlier this season and amid the program's quest for a 10th consecutive SEC title .

Skinner has also led the Wildcats to 21 consecutive NCAA Tournaments, highlighted by the 2020 national title.

"Coach Skinner represents the type of excellence we want Kentucky Athletics to stand for," Batt said in a press release. "He has built a championship program, developed outstanding student-athletes, attracted record crowds and created an expectation to compete at the highest level year after year. We're bullish about where Kentucky Athletics is headed, and volleyball is a great example why. Craig has built something special here, and we're excited about what's ahead for the program."

"Since Megan and I arrived in Lexington in 2005, Kentucky has become our home and embraced us with open arms," Skinner said in a press release. "We've won championships together, we've watched athletes become leaders as they graduate, and we've done it all with the support of Big Blue Nation by our side. We are thrilled to be a part of J's long-term vision for Kentucky Athletics. We're excited about our staff and continuing to build on the foundation that we've created alongside the momentum in the sport of volleyball. Thank you to President Capilouto, J Batt, Rachel Newman Baker and Katie Eiserman for their trust in me and continued support of Kentucky Volleyball, and let's go finish 2026 strong!"

articles.title: Auburn football surges in USA TODAY re-rank after upsetting Georgia
articles.summary: Auburn football climbs 12 spots in the latest re-rank from USA TODAY Sports after a major upset win over top-ranked Georgia.
articles.body:
The Auburn Tigers became the second team in as many weeks to upset the top-ranked team as an unranked squad when they downed Georgia on the road last Saturday.

Auburn's hard work met opportunity last Saturday, and many outlets are starting to buy stock in the Tigers. USA TODAY's Paul Myerberg is one of those. Myerberg boosted Auburn in his weekly college football re-rank , sliding the Tigers up 12 spots to No. 26 after its upset win over Georgia. The loss sent Georgia to No. 4 behind Miami, Ohio State, and BYU. Myerberg's top four mirrors the latest US LBM Coaches Poll.

The win over Georgia pushes Auburn to its highest ranking in Myerberg's weekly feature. Auburn's previous high was No. 30 after the Week 4 win over Vanderbilt , and Auburn has risen 37 spots from its No. 63 preseason ranking .

Three of Auburn's final six opponents are in the re-rank's top 25 this week, including this week's opponent. The LSU Tigers rank No. 21 after shutting out Mississippi State last weekend. Auburn will also face No. 7 Ole Miss and No. 16 Alabama in the top 25, while Mississippi State ranks No. 27 and Arkansas checks in at No. 85. Samford, Auburn's FCS opponent, is not included in Myerberg's weekly re-rank.

Auburn will look to boost its stock again this Saturday when it faces LSU at Jordan-Hare Stadium. Kickoff is set for 11 a.m. CT on ABC.

articles.title: Brewers' beloved catcher gets trade outlook that might be brutal reality check for fans
articles.summary: This would be a harsh dose of reality for the Brewers this upcoming offseason.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers are facing off against the Tampa Bay Rays in the MLB World Series. With a realistic chance of winning their first-ever World Series, all of the focus is on the present, not the future.

But, the reason why the Brewers have been able to get to the World Series is the shrewd business they conduct. Milwaukee isn't afraid of making controversial moves, especially when it comes to trades, if it's for the betterment of the franchise.

MLB insider Robert Murray of Fansided.com highlighted another player who could be on the move, as beloved catcher Williams Contreras is a name to watch this offseason on the trade block.

Williams Contreras tabbed as trade candidate for Brewers

"Contreras will be entering the last year of his deal in 2027, and with so many teams needing catching, he will surely draw trade interest," Murray writes.

Contreras, like Freddy Peralta, Corbin Burnes, Josh Hader, and Devin Williams before him, could be traded this offseason heading into the final year of his deal.

It worked out great with Peralta, and some of those other moves netted some valuable players as well. Milwaukee isn't afraid of trading a beloved player if it helps the team long-term.

Unfortunately, that might be the case this upcoming offseason. Even if the Brewers wind up winning the World Series and Contreras plays a huge role, he could still be traded.

Teams around baseball need catching help, and the Brewers could land a massive haul for even just one year of Contreras in a trade.

Whether it's a combination of prospects or big-league talent, the Brewers are sure to get some strong offers from clubs interested in acquiring Contreras, especially if they make him available.

This trade update from Murray is a brutal reality check for the Brewers fanbase, as even though they might not ever want to see Contreras go, this franchise has shown time and time again that they're willing to trade valuable players in the final year of their deal.

Will Contreras be different and sign an extension? It remains to be seen. But one thing is clear: Contreras isn't locked into a future with the Brewers once the 2026 MLB World Series comes to a close, even if he's a key reason why they win it all.
